#726. Four Midlands teams in the Championship top five - can it last?

Mark Robins (Stoke City), Cesar Peixoto (Wolves), Chris Davies (Birmingham City) and James Morrison (West Bromwich Albion) all have cause to feel content

It is beginning to look a lot like Christmas for followers of Midlands football.

Granted, it is actually only November, but with more than a third of the 2026-27 Championship season gone, already the table is taking on an increasingly familiar weekly look in terms of the primary promotion contenders.

There has been many a year when there have been early-season stirrings in the Midlands, only for the momentum to fade.

But Coventry City proved it can be done after 25 years away from the Premier League. And now Stoke City, Wolves, Birmingham City and West Bromwich Albion are all in contention to join both the Sky Blues and Aston Villa in the top flight.

Stoke in second, Wolves third, Blues fourth and Albion fifth makes for both a heartening, yet surprising sight, with only Middlesbrough in front of them.

It is only six months since Wolves were relegated and, for all the summer discontent at Molineux and doubts among disillusioned fans about their worthiness as serious candidates, the fact is they are very much in the mix.

But, while most people at Molineux can now at least contemplate a quick return, for their local rivals the parachute payments have long since expired.

Blues have been away the longest, their 15-year absence from the top flight having even included a one-season return to the third tier and back.

But, given their extensive American backing, the club have ambitions to be serious contenders - and the only surprise was that it took so long to find their feet.

For Stoke and Albion to be up there was not necessarily forecast, but it has made for all the more happy motoring for the BBC correspondents who cover the quartet of clubs on a regular basis.

BBC Sport asked reporters from BBC Stoke & Staffordshire and BBC West Midlands Sport for their analysis of the season so far and what lies in store for each club...

Next five fixtures: Millwall (H), West Ham (A), QPR (H), Lincoln (A), West Brom (H)

Championship finishes since last in the Premier League: 16th, 15th, 14th, 14th, 16th, 17th, 18th, 17th

American midfielder Jack McGlynn (centre, smiling) is Stoke's top scorer, having hit Championship goals in 10 starts for Stoke, shading the three from defender Ben Wilmot (right)

Mark Elliott, BBC Radio Stoke commentator

Mark Robins has spoken a lot about evolution and incremental gains in his time as Stoke City manager, but it's hard to escape the feeling that there's been a full-blown revolution over the past three months.

Stoke began the season with three defeats, a manager under pressure and the impending loss of their most productive player in Sorba Thomas - but a change in formation, an excellent summer transfer window and an unbelievable run of form has quietened all dissenting voices.

Thirty two out of a possible 39 points from 13 games since the window closed is a brilliant record - but Stoke are maybe still short of truly turning the hopefully optimistic among their fans into true believers.

Most of that is a hangover from last season's promising start eventually falling apart, but there are substantial differences.

The squad has more quality and depth, a more ambitious way of playing and the less quantifiable qualities of tenacity and resilience and a mental strength that, coupled with defensive solidity, has allowed them to find multiple ways to win close games.

Luke Graham, Ethan Galbraith, Jack McGlynn and Ben Johnson have been their most eye-catching summer acquisitions but several who struggled last season, Eric Bocat first among them, have found success too.

The next step is to create more chances and score more goals, whilst maintaining anything close to their current return of points per game.

Even the most hardened pessimists will then maybe see a play-off place as a realistic aim for 2027.

Next five fixtures: Derby (H), Lincoln (A), Southampton (H), QPR (A), Millwall (H)

Championship finishes since last in the Premier League: Relegated (2026)

In-form Adam Armstrong's strike at Wrexham was part of a run of four goals in five games

Only a point behind, and with the feeling they have not played to their full ability very often yet - not very often for 90 consecutive minutes, certainly - Wolves are not badly placed.

Their supporters can be hard taskmasters at the moment, and can hardly be blamed for that in view of the mess of recent seasons and the big promises made of going full-tilt to get straight back up.

For all the understandable misgivings, though, there is a clear path towards achieving it.

Reaching the end of that path may require some judicious spending in January to tidy up a squad that still looks imbalanced, with a surfeit of players in some areas and a shortage in others.

Personal surges in form, from Fer Lopez early in the season to Adam Armstrong more recently, have covered up the gaps and reminded everyone that this squad is not short of class at this level.

Cesar Peixoto, new to England, has handled a delicate situation in a tumultuous league with quiet confidence.

He will have to complete the job in May before he can claim credit more widely, but appears to realise the power he can harness if, like a certain Portuguese predecessor, he can unify all the forces around the club to point in the same direction.

Wolves' Mane of the moment has to now kick on

Next five fixtures: Burnley (A), Bolton (H), Charlton (A), Watford (H), Portsmouth (A)

Finishes since last in the Premier League: Fourth (lost to Blackpool in play-offs), 12th, 21st, 10th, 10th, 19th, 19th, 17th, 20th, 18th, 20th, 17th, 22nd, League One champions, 10th

Blues top scorer August Priske has netted six goals in 12 starts this season

For all of the outside noise about the future of Chris Davies, the Birmingham City board have steadfastly backed their man. Now that decision is paying dividends.

Thanks to that rarely tried footballing trait of continuity, they spent the international break sitting at the top of a very congested Championship table.

But Saturday's 1-0 loss against 10-man Stoke was a reminder of just how tight the division is.

The reboot of the squad started in earnest in January, when the future for Davies was at its wobbliest.

The Â£18m-plus combined investment in Colombian midfielder Jhon Solis, Danish striker August Priske and Spanish winger Carlos Vicente gave them a chance to bed in to English football over the second half of this season, before kicking on this time around.

Priske, at 22, has a high ceiling. His six Championship goals this season has come with improved physicality and increased confidence.

The industry and physique of Solis have stabilised Blues midfield, while Vicente is one of four options on the wing following the loan addition of Liam Millar.

Davies himself has learned from his first Championship season. His team are now versatile, more able to move the ball forward quickly, no longer wedded to possession at all costs.

Defensively too there is a greater resilience and a visible hunger to succeed.

Whether they are serious contenders for automatic promotion remains to be seen, but they have the ingredients to retain a top six spot over the full 46-game course."

Little solace - and no Solis - in setback at Stoke

Next five fixtures: Bolton (A), Bristol City (H), Portsmouth (A), Cardiff (H), Stoke (A)

Championship finishes since last in Premier League: 10th, ninth, fifth, ninth, 21st

Northern Ireland international Isaac Price is having a fine season for both club and country

James Morrison's mind was at ease over this international break following Albion's 3-0 win over Millwall.

He is refusing to reveal any pre-season expectations, but looking at the Championship table makes for satisfying reading.

Certainly externally, nobody expected the Baggies to be fifth - just one point off the automatic promotion places - a third into this campaign.

Morrison has now racked up 51 points from 30 league games in charge. That includes his three interim spells, although the second was a single game as head coach in the FA Cup in January against their next opponents, Swansea City - in between the dismal reigns of Ryan Mason and Eric Ramsay.

It is wild to think of the difference Morrison and his excellent coaching staff have made in 2026.

Albion were heading in the direction of League One when the key were handed to the club legend, who'd been in the back seat the entire time.

A 10-game unbeaten run steered them to safety, and he even had to navigate a points deduction from the EFL for a breach of financial rules.

The club is in a much better place on and off the field, with Mozza now firmly at the wheel.

The upcoming January transfer window could play a big part in determining whether they continue on this positive path, but Baggies fans are at least enjoying the ride again.

#725. Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future

Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

"Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp said, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves."

The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

It paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

The 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

"I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp said after the Netherlands match.

"We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired."

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

But Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," said Klopp.

Scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

"A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still said it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong."

Proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he said, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer."

While that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

"We've been through a tough time," he said. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it."

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

"We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he said.

In Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

#724. Barnet forward Noel-Williams charged with rape

Isiah Noel-Williams has been remanded in custody

League Two footballer Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged with rape.

Noel-Williams, who plays for League Two side Barnet, has been charged with three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault by penetration, Hertfordshire Police said.

The 23-year-old, of High Oaks, St Albans, was remanded in custody following a hearing at Hatfield Magistrates' Court on Saturday.

In a statement, the club said it was "co-operating fully with authorities" and would determine further action "in due course".

Noel-Williams has also been charged with one count of engaging in sexual communication with a child, and one count of supplying a controlled (Class B) drug, police added.

In a statement, the London club said: "Barnet FC can confirm that first-team player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged and remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary.

"The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.

"As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment."

Noel-Williams, who previously played for Hemel Hempstead Town, Kettering Town, Matlock Town, Harrow Borough and Cheshunt, joined Barnet in June.

#723. Villa beaten late on at Galatasaray as winless run continues

Galatasaray vs Aston Villa. UEFA Champions League Round 1.

Match report as Deniz Gul's strike beats Aston Villa in the Champions League league phase, with Galatasaray winning 1-0; the game lacked chances, with Villa failing to score for a second game in a row; Unai Emery's side have not won in six matches

Aston Villa's winless run extended to six games as a late Deniz Gul's header saw them beaten 1-0 by Galatasaray in the Champions League league phase.

It is the first time Villa have lost back-to-back league phase or group games under Unai Emery, putting them in a perilous position ahead of tough games against PSG and Borussia Dortmund in their next two European fixtures.

The Premier League side have not won since beating Manchester City on October 24, and have not scored since Leon Goretzka's strike against Manchester United on November 8.

It was a game that lacked chances, and it took until the 79th minute - Gul's goal - for a shot on target. Villa failed to deal with a corner, with Nicolas Jackson's poor attempted clearance landing to the Galatasaray forward, who nodded home for his first Champions League goal.

Aston Villa failed to attempt a shot on target in this game, it's the first time they failed to attempt a shot on target in a game in the UEFA Champions League (since at least 2004/2005).

He took a boot to the face from Jackson with the Villa forward attempting to clear. There was a VAR check for a possible red card, but nothing was given.

In contrast to Emery's side, Galatasaray extend their winning run to eight games in all competitions ahead of the Istanbul derby against Besiktas on Monday. They move up to 13th in the league phase table, and have now won three successive Champions League games - matching a club record.

Aston Villa dropped into ninth by the end of Tuesday's matches on goal difference and could do so further by the end of matchday five. They play away to Ipswich next, live on Saturday Night Football.

#721. Why Potts swapped West Ham for Club Brugge after 16 years

Freddie Potts has started all of Club Brugge's Champions League games

When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.

The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisclosed fee.

And he has started every game, bar one missed through suspension, in all competitions.

After losing to Aston Villa in the Champions League, they have defeated Inter Milan, Lens and PSV.

"It really is a dream because you hear the music and then you see your family in the stands and you remember all the times that you watched Champions League on TV," Potts told BBC Radio 5 Live's Euro Leagues Show.

"You think of all the memories that you make watching it and to be playing in it now is something that every kid dreams of."

Potts' whole life had been based around West Ham. He had been with the club since the age of six and his father Steve, who made 506 appearances for the Hammers, is a first-team coach.

Potts Jr played 28 times for West Ham, with 25 of them coming last season as they were relegated from the Premier League.

He also had loan spells with Wycombe in League One and Portsmouth in the Championship.

"In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren't as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said 'let's explore options because this season I'm 22, turning 23'," Potts said.

"It's a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn't really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

"I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.

"It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It's been the right decision for me and so far I'm enjoying it, I'm loving life here."

Club Brugge won the Belgian title last season and are second, just one point behind leaders Union Saint-Gilloise this campaign.

"It's a physical league," said Potts. "My running and physical stats have been higher than they've ever been. It's a demanding league in that way.

"Club Brugge demands a lot, from winning the ball back and going man for man in the press. And your responsibility off the ball is something that you have to take really seriously."

Freddie Potts on leaving West Ham, life in Belgium and beating Inter Milan

Potts says he has not started to learn French or Flemish and that team talks are done in English, with the side managed by Croat Ivan Leko.

And he revealed he has a lifelong history with the city.

"The whole move itself is funny because we used to visit Brugge when I was a kid," he said.

"We used to come around Christmas, so my family all know the city. And now I'm here they come out as much as they can.

"It's a great city with a lot of culture. It's brilliant. You won't find many places like it."

Next up for the side is the visit of Liverpool this week - with both clubs on nine points after four games.

The Reds are eighth and Club Brugge are ninth in the table.

"Everyone knows Liverpool as a club, the size and the Premier League teams," said Potts, who started for West Ham at home to the Reds last season.

"It's going to be a big game. We're level on points in the Champions League and we've put big performances in this competition and we're hoping that we're going to do the same."

#720. Oxford beat Spurs U21s to seal EFL Trophy progress

Aaron Ramsey is experiencing the EFL Trophy for the first time in his football career

Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United beat Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1 to secure one of the final two Jersey Mike's Trophy knockout spots.

Oxford knew avoiding defeat by a margin of four goals or more would be enough to seal progression from Southern Group A alongside already-qualified Exeter City.

They trailed to Tyler Tingey's early opener on Tuesday, which gave Spurs' youngsters a glimmer of hope of pulling off that mini-miracle.

But Jun'ai Byfield's own goal and 18-year-old Jack Lee's late winner ensured ex-Arsenal man Ramsey got one over his old north London rivals as Oxford won to finish top of the group.

Elsewhere, Fleetwood's decisive Northern Group G match at home to Leeds United Under-21s was put back 24 hours because of a waterlogged pitch.

The two sides will now meet on Wednesday to decide who progresses alongside group leaders Oldham Athletic to complete the line-up for the knockout stages.

There were wins for League Two pair Tranmere Rovers and Salford City over Premier League sides in Tuesday's other two ties, which were virtually dead rubbers.

Tranmere, who had already sealed their last-32 spot, came from behind to beat eliminated Everton Under-21s 2-1 with goals from David Kamara and Charlie Veevers in Northern Group E.

Both Salford City and Sunderland Under-21s had already been eliminated from Northern Group A but goals from Paolo Mariani, Brandon Cooper and Kyrell Malcolm gave the Ammies a 3-2 win despite Jaydon Jones' Black Cats double.

Of the 16 Premier League under-21 sides to enter the competition, with one placed in each group, only six have progressed to the knockout rounds, although Leeds can still make that number seven.

The last-32 draw will take place on Wednesday at 16:30 GMT. Ties will take place in the week commencing 7 December.

All 16 group winners are guaranteed a home tie, with fixtures remaining regionalised until the semi-final stage.

#719. FA chief signs NDA to view Fifa sell-off plot documents

Debbie Hewitt has been chair at the FA since 2022

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.

Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".

Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.

Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'â¦ which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".

They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".

The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.

Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.

"As a member association, the FA is entitled to hold the Fifa president accountable for his actions, and as a Fifa Council vice-president, Hewitt should have seen these plans as soon as they were hatched.

"They had the right to demand to see these documents, and should have exercised that right forcefully and publicly, rather than signing a gagging clause that puts Fifa and Infantino back in control."

115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

Hewitt has previously criticised Infantino for a lack of transparency.

However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.

It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.

Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.

Fifa has been approached for comment. Sources have previously indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

#718. Rob Lowe Makes Rare Comment About His Sex Tape Scandal

Decades after Rob Lowe's sex tape with a woman and a teenage girl—whom he said he believed was at least 21—was leaked, he reflected on the scandal in his new doc Rob Lowe: The Outsider.

Rob Lowe is looking back at a difficult chapter.

Nearly 40 years after the Parks and Rec actor was at the center of a sex tape scandal involving a then 22-year-old woman and a 16-year-old girl, he shared insight into the devastating toll it took on him.

"I'm not trying to do revisionist history, but we were in an over-21 bar," Lowe recalled in his new Netflix documentary Rob Lowe: The Outsider. "I'm a known film actor, and I had to show my ID to get in. I had no idea that one of the girls was underage."

The St. Elmo's Fire star, then 24—who eventually settled a lawsuit with the teen's family out of court and was not charged with a crime—knew that there was always a possibility that filming his encounter with the women could "get out." (Though the age of consent in Georgia, where the encounter took place, is 16, filming a person under 18 engaging in sexual activity is a federal crime.)

"People would ask me to pay a lot of money to try to keep the tape quiet, and I was unwilling to be blackmailed," he shared before sardonically asking, "Boy, I showed them, didn't I?"

When the video did leak in 1989, one year after it was filmed, Lowe learned he was "leading the news" while attending Cannes Film Festival to announce his 1990 film Bad Influence.

"I was advised by Hollywood's finest to not defend myself, so I didn't because they're the experts," he said of the sex tape's aftermath. "As everything began to explode around me, I just hunkered down. Like I stayed in my house. I didn't leave my house."

Since the scandal coincided with the promotion of his movie—which also starred James Spader and Marcia Cross—Lowe faced a barrage of questions about the incident.

"You'd go promote the movie, and you'd get an entire interview and then they go, 'Let me just, one thing I wanna ask you,'" he explained. "I just kind of soldiered on."

As the West Wing star struggled in the aftermath—which included an ill-fated Oscars opening ceremony performance—it was hosting Saturday Night Live in 1990 that ultimately changed the trajectory of his life. Now, he was laughing with the public, rather than just being laughed at.

"Whenever a public figure gets in trouble, Lorne Michaels comes a-callin,'" he explained. "They called me right after the video broke and wanted me to come on and do a bit. I said, 'Call me back when you want me to host.'"

And soon, Lowe found himself at Rockefeller Center's famed Studio 8H alongside the likes of Mike Myers, Dana Carvey and Nora Dunn.

"I was willing to stand in the fire and take my slings for a good laugh, and it wasn't meant as a rehabilitation," he clarified. "To me, it was really, I got a chance to host Saturday Night Live, which is something I'd been wanting to do forever."

Though Lowe—who shares sons Matthew Lowe, 33, and John Owen Lowe, 31, with wife Sheryl Berkoff—has expressed immense regret about the sex tape over the years, he previously revealed that the incident helped him reprioritize his life.

"It's not a great recipe for success to give an 18-year-old male fame, money, drugs," the actor—who got sober in 1990 after a years-long struggle with alcohol and cocaine—said on SiriusXM in 2019, "and expect there not to be something that goes wrong."

"It got me sober, sober got me married," he added. "I've been married 29 years and I have two great sons. I don't think any of that happens without going through that scandal."

For a closer look at more celebrities who've shared insight into their own sobriety journeys, keep reading.

After the two-time NBA champ was arrested and charged with a DUI in January 2026, he became informed on how to fight against his addictions.

“If you do your education, addiction [is where] you suffer from a brain disease, just like cancer or any other disease," he said during an appearance on Page Six Radio that April. "I don't think anyone would wish to have cancer.”

Lamar added, “So, me being educated on disease, the more and more I get educated, the more and more it's easier for me to stay sober.”

The basketball star—who survived a near-fatal drug overdose in 2015—had previously detailed the inspiration he hopes to be to others after passing 60 days of being "completely sober."

“I have a certain type of mental and physical endurance, but when it comes to getting high and escaping, I'm just like everyone else,” he told USA Today in March 2026. “If I could just help the average person and give them faith and hope that they can overcome it, then that's probably one of the reasons why the Lord spared me.”

In October 2018, the American Pie star announced he was one year sober in a celebratory and encouraging Instagram post.

“I first tried to get sober over 5 years ago, when the weight of my obsession with booze and drugs became too heavy for me to handle,” he wrote at the time. “Turns out this s--t is hard.”

He continued, “After some fits and starts, I’ve managed to put together one year of sobriety. I’m as proud of it as anything in my life. If you’re struggling, know there’s help. Don’t be ashamed. We can do this.”

Years later, he reflected on his journey with addiction and the lengths he went to hide the his struggle.

“I’m going to therapy and ‘working on things’ but meanwhile I’m leaving therapy, having just had a good session, and I’m going to the liquor store and buying a fifth of vodka, drinking it and then driving home,” he said on a March 2024 episode of his wife Jenny Mollen's All the Fails podcast. “I knew how to get wasted enough to where I took myself out of the life equation, took myself out of the present, didn’t have to connect in a way that made me feel things.”

He added, “I had it figured out to a T. To not get too drunk where I couldn’t have a conversation with you. I was replacing those bottles in the bar all the time.”

The two-time FIFA Women's World Cup champ has been open about her misuse of Adderall while battling injuries during her college soccer career.

“I was getting really heavily addicted to Adderall and misusing it,” she said on a 2025 episode of the Question Everything with Danielle Robay podcast. “I was taking it all the time. I would go days without sleeping. It was wild. I felt like I was gonna give myself a heart attack. I was crushing it. I was snorting it. It was so problematic.”

However, in the midst of her struggle, her college coach Anson Dorrance was there to support her.

“It got really, really dark and I had to make some serious adjustments,” she explained, “and Anson would have me read books. I started reading this book called [Man’s Search] for Meaning and it's about suffering and reframing it and it changed my life.”

In October 2025, the Migos member shared he was four years sober from codeine—an opioid used to make the soda-based drink sizzurp—after a "wake-up call" from his teenage son Jordan.

"My oldest son kept asking for like pineapple Fanta, but he don't even really drink soda," Offset recounted on Baby, This Is Keke Palmer. "And then one day he came in studio like, ‘Why yours is different color than mine?’ It killed me."

Explaining how the innocuous remark "touched" a nerve, Offset continued, "When I went in my room, I damn near cried."

Over the years, the two-time Oscar winner has spoken candidly about December 29, 1975: the day he got sober.

“I was drunk and driving my car here in California in a blackout,” he revealed in October 2025 on the New York Times podcast The Interview podcast, “no clue where I was going, when I realized that I could have killed somebody—or myself, which I didn’t care about—and I realized that I was an alcoholic.”

After reaching out to a friend for help, he was able to begin a new path. And in December 2025, he reached 50 years of sobriety, doing so with a message to those in a similar position he found himself in a half century ago.

“Choose life instead of the opposite,” he said in an Instagram message. “Life life life and more life.”

The Valley star shared his decades-long battle with drugs in March 2025 after going to rehab.

"I am coming out that I'm an addict," Jax shared during the March 4 episode of Bravo's Hot Mic podcast. "I have substance issues, primarily with cocaine. It’s hard to say out loud."

"I’ve been dealing with this on and off since I was 23 and now I’m 45," he continued. "There was times where I would stop doing it but then there were times where I’d go heavy on it.”

Jax also gave up drinking, explaining, "I don’t necessarily think I have an alcohol problem, but the two go hand in hand. I can’t do cocaine without drinking. So, I just gave up both. I’m proud to say I’m 82, 83 days sober right now, which is the longest I’ve ever gone in my life without either.”

The Spider-Man: No Way Home star stopped drinking alcohol in 2022 after feeling "enslaved" to the drink. "I was definitely addicted to alcohol, not shying away from that at all," Holland recalled on the On Purpose with Jay Shetty podcast. "I think that anyone that has a beer everyday has probably got a little bit of a problem."

"And then you would just reach that moment where you're like 'Wow, I shouldn't have had that last beer,'" the actor continued. "And you wake up the next day and you have a terrible headache."

Since making the lifestyle change, Holland noticed he "could sleep better" and "handle problems better."

"Things that would go wrong on set that would normally set me off, I could take in my stride," he shared. "I had so much such better mental clarity. I felt healthier. I felt fitter."

The star of Hunt for Red October does not often speak to his sobriety journey, which began almost forty years ago.

"I don't discuss this a lot," he said during a May 2024 podcast appearance. "I discuss it every now and then when it makes sense. I'm 39 years sober. I got sober Feb. 23, 1985."

Speaking about his life after moving from New York City to Los Angeles in 1983, Alec explained, "I had a white-hot problem every day for two years. I think I snorted a line of cocaine from here to Saturn. We took it back home. I mean, cocaine was like coffee back then. Everybody was doing it all day long."

And after quitting the drug, he soon turned to alcohol—only to also quit that dependency.

"New York relaxes me," he shared of his home. "I walk around and I see aspects of it that I've never seen before. I'll look at a building and I'll go, 'My God, I never noticed that about that building, those doors.' I have lunches and coffee and my friends."

The Princess Diaries alum shared in April 2024 that she is more than five years sober. As she told the New York Times, "That feels like a milestone to me."

Her reasoning was clear. "I knew deep down it wasn't for me," she shared. "And it just felt so extreme to have to say, 'But none?' But none. If you're allergic to something or have an anaphylactic reaction to something, you don't argue with it. So I stopped arguing with it."

And she's happy she made that decision. "My personal experience with it is that everything is better," she continued. "For me, it was wallowing fuel. And I don't like to wallow."

While accepting the 2018 Woman of the Year Award by the Peggy Albrecht Friendly House, a residential program for women recovering from substance and alcohol abuse, Moore spoke about the "self-destructive path" that nearly derailed her career.

"I feel like there's a defining moments in our lives that shape who we are and the direction we go and early in my career, I was spiraling down a path of real self-destruction and no matter what successes I had, I just never felt good enough," the star recalled. "I had absolutely no value for myself and this self-destructive path, it very quickly brought me to a real crisis point and it wasn't clear at the time the reason. Maybe it was divine intervention."

Moore, who sought treatment in 2012, thanked two unnamed people she "barely knew" for delivering something of an ultimatum to her to turn her life around. "Unless I was dead, I better show up," she quipped, adding that she was given "a chance to redirect the course of my life before I destroyed everything."

"Clearly they saw more of me than I saw of myself," Moore noted. "And I'm so grateful because without that opportunity, without their believing me, I wouldn't be standing here today."

Cyrus shared in 2022 that she's been in recovery for her Xanax addiction since 2020. "It gave me so much structure in the time that I really needed structure, because I didn't want to just be sitting around and stirring in my brain," she told Rolling Stone. "It gave me hope."

The singer added, "Once I felt that it was possible to silence things out for a second and numb your pain, it was over."

She said her friends at the time "kind of cosigned" her drug use and "it just kind of becomes this dark pit, bottomless pit." But, during the pandemic, Cyrus said she was noticing challenges and felt she wasn't emotionally present. "I was completely nodding off and falling asleep," she recalled. "And unable to keep my head up or keep my eyes open, because I was so far gone."

She eventually sought help and noted that "it took some time to get on my own two feet."

The "Lose Yourself" rapper reflected on his prior prescription pill abuse in his 2025 documentary Stans, noting an overdose and missing his daughter Hailie Jade's birthday party prompted a change.

“I cried because it was like, ‘Oh my god, I missed that,’” he said in the doc. “I kept saying to myself, ‘Do you want to f--king miss this again? Do you want to miss everything? If you can’t do it for yourself, you f--king pussy, at least do it for them.’”

Eventually, channeling his energy back into his music helped the Oscar winner on his sobriety journey.

“It did something. It turned the light on,” he explained. “I realized I’m not embarrassed anymore about [sobriety]. I started treating sobriety like a super power and I took pride in the fact that I was able to quit.”

The Parenthood alum was sober for 16 years before relapsing in 2020 by taking Vicodin after a motorcycle accident.

"For the last eight weeks maybe, I don't really know…I'm on them all day," he said on his Armchair Expert podcast. "And I'm allowed to be on them at some dosage because I have a prescription and then I'm also augmenting that."

"And I hate it," he continued. "And I'm lying to other people. And I know I have to quit. But my tolerance is going up so quickly that I'm now in a situation where I'm taking, you know, eight 30s a day, and I know that's an amount that's going to result in a pretty bad withdrawal. And I start getting really scared, and I'm starting to feel really lonely. And I just have this enormous secret."

In 2018, the Halloween star got very candid about her 10-year addiction to opiates, which began in the late '80s after a minor plastic surgery "for my hereditary puffy eyes." The reslt was a prescription that changed her life. "I had a 10-year run, stealing, conniving," she told People. "No one knew. No one."

When her sister visited her in the summer of 1998 and brought along prescribed painkillers for a rib injury, Curtis said she hit her rock bottom. "I knew she had them in her suitcase in our guest room closet," she told the publication, crying at the memory. "I basically took all her opiates. When she was leaving I knew she would pack her suitcase and find her pills missing. I knew I had to acknowledge to her what I had done, and so I wrote her a note and left it on her suitcase. I came home that day, and she put her arms around me and told me she loved me and she was concerned about me and she was unwilling to watch me kill myself."

She attended her first meeting on Feb. 3, 1999, the same day she revealed her struggle to her filmmaker husband Christopher Guest. "He was incredulous that he'd never noticed," Curtis said, adding that she's been sober ever since.

Barrymore, who previously went to rehab for alcohol and drug addiction, shared in 2021 that she was marking a big milestone in her journey. "I'm just going to say something for the first time in a long time: I have not had a drink of alcohol in two and a half years," she said on CBS Mornings. "And it was something that I realized just did not serve me in my life."

She added, "It's so funny. When we reveal ourselves and our truths and the things we've worked so hard for, it's so liberating and vulnerable all at the same time."

Barrymore later explained to the Los Angeles Times that she doesn't use the "sober" label because she doesn't want people to think she's "some perfect Puritan."

"I kept thinking, ‘I'll master this. I'll figure it out,'" she said in 2023. "And finally, I just realized: ‘You've never mastered this, and you never will.'"

The A Star Is Born actor struggled with a cocaine addiction during the early aughts before friend Will Arnett stepped in and confronted him out about his behavior.

"That was the first time I ever realized I had a problem with drugs and alcohol⁠," Cooper recalled during a 2022 appearance on the Smartless podcast. "I'll just never forget it."

Crediting Arnett as "the reason" he went sober, Cooper added, "He took that risk of having a hard conversation with me that put me on a path of deciding to change my life."

The Fight Club star spent years struggling with alcohol before Cooper helped him get sober. "I got sober because of this guy," he told the audience at the 2020 National Board of Review Annual Awards after Cooper presented him with a trophy. "And every day's been happier ever since."

In September 2023, the Cruel Intentions alum shared on Instagram that this was "the longest I've gone since I was a teen without some kind of nicotine or marijuana in my system (among other things)."

"Feeling thankful for the freedom that comes with breaking addictions and dependency on substance," he added. "Sobriety, clarity, and spiritual connectedness feels real good."

After publicly celebrating six years of sobriety on tour in 2018, the singer stunned fans later that same year with the release of the confessional single "Sober," which revealed that she had relapsed.

"Mama, I'm so sorry I'm not sober anymore / And Daddy please forgive me for the drinks spilled on the floor / To the ones who never left me / We've been down this road before I'm so sorry, I'm not sober anymore," she sang.

A month later, Lovato was hospitalized for a near-fatal overdose.

"I have always been transparent about my journey with addiction," she wrote on Instagram two weeks later. "What I've learned is that this illness is not something that disappears or fades with time. It is something I must continue to overcome and have not done yet...I now need time to heal and focus on my sobriety and road to recovery. The love you have all shown me will never be forgotten and I look forward to the day where I can say I came out on the other side. I will keep fighting."

In 2018, she recalled battling her addictions to sex and alcohol. "My sort of addictions jump. They jump around. When I was younger, I definitely think I had a sex addiction of some kind, yes, that everything could be fixed by sex," she said, before sharing about the time she realized she'd developed a troubling drinking problem.

"I remember reaching a rock bottom that time I was in the house by myself and I had those two bottles of wine and was going for the third bottle," she said. "And I was like, ‘Now hold up. You're in the this house by yourself going onto your third bottle of wine? You might have a problem.'"

"So I went cold turkey. That's the thing about me: I can go cold turkey. I am a binger, and I always have to watch myself and I can just get obsessed with things," she continued. "It's not what you're doing but how you're with it. Why you're doing it. It's the behavior that's attached to it because if you want to have a lot of sex, that's great, but why are you having all that sex? That's what you've got to look at."

The Backstreet Boys member tried drugs for the first time before filming the music video for 2000's "The Call," telling Good Morning America years later that he "was off the walls" during the shoot. He got sober in 2021 following a relapse and saw numerous positive benefits just one year later, including losing 32 pounds in seven months by cutting out alcohol and fast food.

"I'm sticking this one out all the way,” he told People in July 2025. "It's a daily thing. But I have finally done what has been suggested amongst the sober community, and my life has flipped in a positive way."

While AJ acknowledged he is "still learning, still growing," he's now confident in who he is.

"I've discovered new verbiage, such as boundaries, never really had those," he continued. "Now I have those, which is a blessing. AJ is a member of a group. He is a persona, but he doesn't define me as an individual. Alexander James is who I am."

After the sudden death of Mac Miller, the rapper—born Shad Moss—took to Twitter to let his fans know that he'd once struggled with a cough syrup addiction. "To the youth- Stop with these dumb ass drugs," he began his series of tweets. "Im going to let something out. When me and Omarion worked on FACE OFF album. I was high off lean everyday! When yall saw me on BET going off on Torae i was high off lean. My attitude everything changed. My fans started to...Turn on me my family too. I never promoted lean in my songs. The whole time i was on the UCP tour with Chris [Brown] I WAS SIPPING 4's atleast 7 times a day. I was addicted until our show in Cincinnati.. i came off stg and passed out woke up in the hospital i was having withdraws.""I never felt a pain like that ever," Bow Wow continued. "It was summer but i was walking round with 3 hoodies on because i was so cold. I missed the chicago show of that tour baltimore show BECAUSE I WAS F--KING HIGH AND SICK!!!! that s--t is not cool and i was doing it to be cool! Kick that s--t! Be a good son or daughter. Be the best you. Ima start being more vocal. We gotta save the youth from going out early. Parents watch your kids. Explain to them. We want yall to live man. I almost died f--king with syrup.""To this day im affected my stomach will...Never be the same and it hasnt been. DRUG FREE IS THE WAY TO BE! smarten up tighten up out here," he told his fans. "We cant lose no more of you. Not one! I love all yall. The young artist all the kids around the world.. dont follow a trend. Break the cycle. PEACE."

With the dual releases of her fourth studio album No Shame and memoir My Thoughts Exactly, the singer spent much of 2018 getting brutally honest about the height of her addition problems. According to Allen, she was abusing cocaine and drinking to the point of being "parisitically drunk. Ultimately, Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin staged an intervention after she accidentally headbutted Orlando Bloom at Kate Hudson's Halloween party and knocked herself out.

She told The Guardian, "Nothing seemed to reach or satisfy me. I remember waking up one morning in those dark days thinking, ‘Maybe it's time for heroin, because nothing else is working.'"

The Parent Trap actor battled a cocaine addiction throughout the '80s that sent him to rehab in 1990. As he later explained on Today, he grew up in the '60s and '70s when "there was a completely different attitude" towards the drug.

"It was even in some movie budgets. I was basically doing cocaine pretty much on a daily basis during the '80s," he admitted in 2018. "I spent many, many a night screaming at God to 'Please take this away from me and I'll never do it again, cause I've only got an hour before I have to be at work.' Then at 4 o'clock in the afternoon I'd go, 'Oh it's not so bad.'"

"I had what I call a white light experience where I saw myself either dead or losing everything that meant anything to me," he continued. He had to sit down then-fiancée Meg Ryan and explain what was going on. Then, he sought help. "That was the end of the love affair with me and cocaine."

After an incident in Newport Beach where the Olympic swimmer tried to kick in his own hotel room door, Lochte made the decision to seek treatment in 2018. "Ryan has been battling from alcohol addiction for many years and unfortunately it has become a destructive pattern for him," his rep told E! News in a statement. "He has acknowledged that he needs professional assistance to overcome his problem and will be getting help immediately."

"Ryan knows that conquering this disease now is a must for him to avoid making future poor decisions, to be the best husband and father he can be, and if he wants to achieve his goal to return to dominance in the pool in his 5th Olympics in Tokyo in 2020," the statement concluded.

Although the Parenthood alum knows that "one of the things that you're not supposed to do is get sober for somebody else," his relationship with now-wife Melanie Lynskey was a major reason that led him to swearing off alcohol.

"At a point, I knew how amazing she was and I thought she would be incredible for someone who deserved her," he explained during a March 2023 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, "and I didn't feel like I was that person. I felt a little bit too crazy."

However, as Ritter noted to E! News, he now sees that sobriety is ultimately a personal choice.

"It was easier for me to say that I'm doing it for her because, at that time, I didn't feel like I was sort of worth much," he recalled of the early days of their relationship. "I didn't care as much about hurting myself as I did about hurting her. So, initially it was easier for me to say, 'I'm doing this for her.' And now, I'm doing it for myself."

The country star has been sober for nearly a decade, but it was a hard-fought road getting there. His addiction to alcohol and pain pills began soon after graduating from high school and didn't abate when his career began to take off. He kept a black leather laptop bag filled with bottles of Jagermeister or vodka "at arm's reach at all times," he told previously revealed to People, adding that throughout the day, "every hour and a half to two hours it'd be time to get two or three good pulls on the bottle. And every three or four hours it's time for a pill or two."

And it had no effect on his success. "It wasn't like I was stumbling around all day," he admitted. "I was fully functioning — I wrote more songs then than I do now. That was the scary part."

In late 2011, he was hospitalized with pancreatitis and was told that if he didn't stop drinking, he wouldn't see his next birthday. "I still put it off and was trying to slow down on my own, like, 'All right I'm only gonna let myself take two pills today. I'm only gonna drink this much of my bottle and make a mark on the bottle,'" he recalled. "And it would work a couple days—and then somebody throws a party."

He eventually sought help, entering rehab on Dec. 18, 2011. "I got to the point where I knew it was something I couldn't do on my own," Gilbert said. "Pissed me off to no end and embarrassed me. I'm a pretty strong-willed person but that was the one thing in my life that I couldn't get to stick."

#717. Klopp advice and Iraola confidence boosts Wirtz

Wirtz moved from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool for Â£116m in 2025

Florian Wirtz says he is enjoying his best form yet at Liverpool and benefiting from Andoni Iraola's confidence and Jurgen Klopp's advice.

Wirtz, 23, scored in Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday and has three goals and six assists this season.

The Germany midfielder made the Â£116m move from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025 and after failing to make his mark in his first campaign in England, is beginning to showcase his quality for Iraola's side.

Speaking in Belgium before Liverpool's Champions League game against Club Brugge, Wirtz said: "I can't really say that I've changed that much.

"I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it."

He also said he has been picking the brains of Germany manager Klopp, the former Liverpool boss, while on international duty.

"He tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here and tries to give me some advice to get successful over here as he has shown how it is done," Wirtz said.

"He can give me some good advice. It's always small things. More private things.

"But he is speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it for a long time."

On the influence of Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot as Liverpool head coach in the summer, Wirtz added: "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football, and I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that.

"I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me."

Liverpool have nine points from their four Champions League games, having won their first three before losing to Fenerbahce in Istanbul this month.

Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are both absent from the travelling squad with injuries, with Iraola confirming that Gakpo will be out for the Merseyside derby this weekend, while adding that it is "difficult to say" for Gravenberch.

#716. Non-league player injured falling down badger hole

Cav Miley has made 17 appearances since joining Chelmsford in the summer

Footballers may be among the fittest athletes in the world of sport, but they are not immune to bizarre injuries.

Dave Beasant famously severed a tendon in his big toe when he dropped a bottle of salad cream, while Rio Ferdinand strained tendons in his knee by lying in one position on the sofa for too long watching television.

The latest inductee into the strange injury hall of fame is Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley.

The 31-year-old midfielder missed the 2-2 draw with Walton and Hersham in the National League South on Saturday after twisting an ankle in training by falling down a badger hole.

Miley returned for the 1-0 home victory over Maidstone United on Monday, after which manager Mark Cooper shed more light on the incident.

"Everyone is telling me it's gone viral, but I told the truth - he fell down a badger hole," Cooper told the club's YouTube channel.

"I was told at the start it was a fox hole, but then the guy at where we train told me it's a badger hole.

"We need to make sure we fill all of them in before we train now."

Miley joined Chelmsford in the summer after spells in the National League with Southend United and Eastleigh.

#715. Sheehan to miss Ireland's Nations Championship finale after two-game ban

Dan Sheehan has been suspended following a 'croc-roll' on Springbok loose forward Marco van Staden in the Nations Championship; he will miss Friday's fifth-place play-off against Australia

Ireland captain Dan Sheehan will miss Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia after being handed a two-game ban for his red card against South Africa.

The forward was initially shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley for a croc roll on Springbok replacement Marco van Staden in the 72nd minute of his country's 20-17 victory in Dublin.

The offence was subsequently upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer.

World Rugby law 9.20d states "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".

Sheehan faced a disciplinary hearing on Monday evening where the panel ruled the incident was a "low entry point" offence and merited a two-week suspension.

The 28-year-old has accepted the sanction and will also miss Leinster's United Rugby Championship meeting with the Ospreys on Friday, December 4.

Typically a hooker, Sheehan started at number eight for the first time at Test level against the world champions.With Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all injured, head coach Andy Farrell now faces another reshuffle at the base of the scrum for the meeting with the Wallabies at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

Ronan Kelleher and Tom Stewart are set to continue as the two hookers in Ireland's matchday 23.

#713. Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens

Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

Representatives of Serbia's student-led movement were sworn in as lawmakers on Tuesday, just over four weeks after they ended Serbia's strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic's 14 years of rule.

The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's new government.

The movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103. The remaining seats belong to ethnic minority parties.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Hundreds gathered outside the parliament building in the capital Belgrade, to show their support for the student-backed lawmakers, most of whom are teachers, professors and other professionals with little or no political experience.

Meanwhile, SNS candidates were met with a negative reaction from the crowd. A woman in the crowd poured yogurt over an SNS member's head as she climbed the steps to the parliament entrance.

According to Serbian media, the newly elected lawmakers have been preparing for their first session for days. They will face veteran opposition politicians, including Aleksandar Vucic, who became the opposition leader after his defeat.

The Students' List will have 90 days to name a prime minister, present their programme and form a government, once the parliament is formed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The movement unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

They pledged to improve healthcare, boost education and double the defense budget, along with many other reforms.

The election of a new parliamentary speaker will also lead to the appointment of a new acting president. The speaker has held the role since Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister.

A snap presidential election must be called by November 27 and held by December 27.

Both parties are expected to put forward presidential candidates, but Vucic cannot seek another term because the constitution limits presidents to two terms in office.

#710. Mariah Carey Claps Back at Online Criticism After Recent Performances

Mariah Carey appeared to address online speculation about her health during a performance in Rio de Janeiro on Nov. 21.

All Mariah Carey wants for Christmas, is to put this topic to rest.

As the queen of the holiday season performed at Farmasi Arena in Rio de Janeiro Nov. 21, she appeared to address speculation surrounding her health following her latest concerts.

“By the way, don’t believe everything you read online,” Carey said in a video shared by fans on social media after the show. “Don’t be making me mad, now.”

The “We Belong Together” singer’s comments shortly followed fan speculation that she was going through some sort of health battle due to the blocking in her recent shows.

“Is Mariah Carey choosing to perform as stiff as possible, or is something going on with her health?” a fan wrote on X earlier this month. “She is 57 and needs assistance to even walk around the stage.”

Another responded to a separate video of Carey—mom to 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe with ex Nick Cannon—appearing to struggle to walk in high heels, “If her health really is bad then she needs to take time off and work on herself.”

But some of Carey’s Lambily quickly hopped in to defend her, even before the Grammy winner herself stepped in. As one fan joked in response to the speculation, “She’s still defrosting!!”

The comment, of course, references Carey’s reign as the queen of the festive season—but she has at least begun to thaw this Christmas by kicking off her latest tour.

“Thank you São Paulo!!” Carey wrote in a Nov. 18 post on social media, alongside picture that featured her decked out in Santa outfits. “What an incredible way to kick off my Christmastime Tour.”

And while Carey has become synonymous for her holiday hit—which was only just this year dethroned as the longest charting Billboard hit by Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas”—she has previously emphasized that it isn’t a fluke and she “really, truly loves the holidays.”

“It’s not fake,” she told Good Morning America of her seasonal spirit in 2023, noting that she loves touring during the winter to ensure her fans have “the merriest of Christmases.”

Even 32 years after she put out the record, Carey isn’t surprised it remains her chart-topper, either. After all, fans being obsessed with it was the point. As she put of writing it back in the early 1990s, “My goal was to do something timeless.”

For more fascinating facts about Carey, keep reading…

1. Mariah Carey was born on March 27, 1970 (we think) to Alfred Roy Carey and Patricia Hickey, who'd been disowned by her family for marrying a man of African-American and Afro-Venezuelan descent. They divorced when Carey was 3.

2. Her name comes from the song "They Call the Wind Maria" from the 1951 Broadway musical Paint Your Wagon. Though it isn't spelled the same, it is pronounced the same.

3. When she was young, her family, which includes two older siblings, was subjected to racist attacks because of her parents' interracial marriage. Their dogs were poisoned and a car was blown up.

"That was the beginning of a nightmare," Patricia told Oprah Winfrey during a 1999 interview with her daughter. "When we were eating one night, someone fired a shot through the window. Luckily, none of the children were in the room."

4. While attending Harborfields High School in Greenlawn, New York, she earned the nickname Mirage because of how often she skipped class. According to her unauthorized 2001 biography by Marc Shapiro, Carey's truancy was of great concern for guidance counselor John Garvey.

"You could talk to her until you were blue in the face, and it didn't do any good," Garvey said in the book. "When you talked to her about it, she'd let you know it wasn't that important in her life because she was going to be a rock star." Carey's response? "I don't blame them for trying to encourage me to do better scholastically because they never saw me sing."

5. While recording her third album Music Box, she and Columbia Records head Tommy Mottola began dating. They tied the knot in a lavish ceremony in June 5, 1993. They eventually separated in 1997, with Carey citing his controlling nature and growing creative differences at the catalyst for their relationship's deterioration.

Carey opened up about the relationship on her E! reality series, Mariah's World, saying "I was with someone at the time that had a lot of control over my life. He was older than me by a lot and had a lot of power and he wanted me to remain away from most people, like sequestered. I had to get permission to leave [the house]…I never thought I would get out of there."

6. The first song she ever composed was written while she was still in high school. Called "Here We Go 'Round Again," Carey has described the track, which was featured on her four-song demo tape, as having a Motown vibe.

7. After graduating high school, she moved into a one-bedroom apartment in Manhattan that she shared with four other female students. She worked as a waitress and a coat check girl while also studying cosmetology—all while pursuing her dreams of a music career.

8. At the age of 2, Carey stunned her mom, a vocal coach and occasional opera singer, by imitating her operatic singing. She began taking singing lessons at 4, developing a voice that would span five octaves—a nearly superhuman feat.

9. After meeting rising pop singer Brenda K. Starr, Carey tagged along as her new friend attended a Christmas party hosted by CBS Records. Starr convinced her to bring along her demo tape, which made its way into the hands of the head of Columbia Records, Mottola. All it took was two songs to convince Mottola to sign her.

10. Carey's debut eponymous album was released on June 12, 1990. She earned two Grammys following its release, including one for Best New Artist, and it made her the first musical act since the Jackson 5 to have their first four singles reach number one.

11. Carey's had a life-long affection for Marilyn Monroe and, in 1999, she paid over $600,000 for the icon's white baby grand piano when it came up for auction at Christie's.

12. After meeting Nick Cannon on the set of her music video for "Bye Bye" in 2008, she began dating the comedian. Within two months, they got married, tying the knot on April 30 in a secret ceremony in the Bahamas. They split in 2014.

13. Though she suffered a miscarriage shortly after marrying Cannon, the couple would welcome twins Moroccan and Monroe in 2011. Monroe was named after Carey's idol, Marilyn Monroe, while Moroccan was named after the décor in the room where his father proposed to his mother.

14. In 2008, Carey got herself into some hot water when she performed in a New Year's Eve concert for the family of Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi. She would later claim to "feel horrible and embarrassed to have participated in the event," with her rep Cindi Berger promising in March 2011 that royalties for her upcoming song "Save The Day" would be donated to charities that create awareness for human rights issues. The song was eventually released in 2020.

15. In 2001, after a bizarre appearance on TRL that involved her showing up unannounced, pushing an ice cream cart, and stripping off her clothes, she spent two weeks recovering in a Connecticut mental hospital, citing extreme exhaustion for her breakdown.

She later revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with bipolar II disorder at the time, but kept her diagnosis private. "I'm just in a really good place right now, where I'm comfortable discussing my struggles with bipolar II disorder," she told People at the time. "I'm hopeful we can get to a place where the stigma is lifted from people going through anything alone. It can be incredibly isolating. It does not have to define you and I refuse to allow it to define me or control me."

16. Just months after her stay in the institution, Carey released Glitter into the world. The film and its soundtrack were such bombs that they prompted Virgin Records to buy her out of her record deal for $50 million. She would sign a contract with Island Records in early 2002, launching the record label MonarC in the process.

17. Glitter isn't the only film Carey has appeared in over the years. She earned some pretty great reviews for her work as a social worker in friend Lee Daniels' award-winning 2009 film Precious. In 2013, she appeared in another Daniels' film, The Butler, playing Hattie Pearl, the mother of the film's titular butler, Cecil Gaines (played by Forest Whitaker).

18. Until 2017 "One Sweet Day," Carey's song with Boyz II Men, was the longest-running number one song in history, with 16 weeks spent atop the Billboard Hot 100 in 1995-96. It shared the honor with Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee's "Despacito," featuring Justin Bieber, for a time before Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" surpassed it in the summer of 2019.

19. According to Page Six, Carey's two Jack Russell terriers only fly first class and each with their own respective staff member. Why? Because they apparently loathe one another.

20. Following a career resurgence with the 2005 release of The Emancipation of Mimi, Carey begun lending her name and likeness to endorsement deals for the first time in her career, beginning with ads for Intel Centrino personal computers. In 2006, after signing a contract with Gillette's "Legs of a Goddess" campaign, Carey reportedly insured her legs for $1 billion.

21. After meeting him through her longtime pal, director Brett Ratner, at a movie premiere in Aspen, Colo., Carey became engaged to Australian businessman James Packer in January 2016.

The billionaire, who formed the joint production company RatPac Entertainment with Ratner, proposed with a 35-carat ring. The engagement was called off by October, as both insinuated the relationship ended because of the other's issues.

22. Carey's classic 1994 album Merry Christmas has sold over 18 million copies worldwide, making it the best-selling Christmas album of all time. 25 years after its release, in late December of 2019, her beloved single "All I Want for Christmas Is You" hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the first time, breaking several records (including longest trip to the top) in the process. While extending her record as the solo artist with the most No. 1 singles on the Hot 100, the achievement also made her the only artist in history to have a No. 1 song in four consecutive decades.

23. Her godmother is Patti LaBelle, and the R&B icon has admitted to slapping her goddaughter around back in the day.

24. After Packer, Carey quickly rebounded with backup dancer Bryan Tanaka, the early stages of their relationship captured by Mariah's World cameras.

25. She does not know Jennifer Lopez. So stop asking her.

#708. Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair

Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.

Since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the company's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America."

Nvidia is calling the new group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

The committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.

The company did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was announced hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great company," he said during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea."

Trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other big tech companies.

Huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing company.

That company, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.
