#707. Dane Cook's Wife Kelsi Taylor Is Pregnant, Expecting First Baby

Dane Cook and Kelsi Taylor—who tied the knot in 2023—shared that she is pregnant with their first baby: “We’ve been bursting with excitement to share this news!”

Dane Cook is preparing for his chapter as dad of the month.

The comedian and wife Kelsi Taylor shared they are expecting their first baby together.

Alongside black-and-white maternity photos, Cook, 54, and Taylor, 28, wrote in a joint Nov. 24 Instagram post that they’ve “been bursting with excitement to share this news!”

They added in reference to a bible verse about an answered prayer for a baby, “1 Samuel 1:27.”

In the first snap, the Good Luck Chuck star and fitness inductor stood beneath a tree as they looked lovingly into each other’s eyes. Meanwhile, Taylor held up a sonagram of their baby as Cook laid a gentle hand on her wrist.

Showing off their playful side, another photo showed the couple cozied up on a couch, while a third picture captured a close-up of Taylor’s baby bump.

Reposting the carousel to her Instagram Stories, Taylor wrote, “So grateful for this beautiful chapter of our lives.”

And Cook would have to agree, sharing on his own Instagram Stories that he’s “feeling so incredible.”

The Employee of the Month alum and Taylor tied the knot in September 2023 at a private estate in O'ahu, Hawaii, after nearly six years of dating.

"Last night I married the girl of my dreams here in Hawaii," Cook shared the day after the wedding on X. "The greatest feeling in the world is knowing you've got the strongest person you could ever imagine by your side and giving them all of your love in return."

He continued, "The years of laughs, adventures and accomplishments we've shared were solidified in front of some of our dearest friends and family during an emotional ceremony. I can't wait to share more but for now just know this. I've never felt this way. It's so wonderful."

It’s also wonderful that the couple can poke fun at their 27-year age gap. In fact, the My Best Friend’s Girl actor included a few wisecracks about their relationship in his 2022 stand-up special Dane Cook: Above It All.

"She saw everything that I was working on for the show," Cook exclusively told E! News at the special’s premiere. "And she was like, ‘Keep that in. I think that part will be great.' There's even some fun at our own expense."

As for why he wanted to draw inspiration from their age difference? "If we can't laugh at it,” he said, "then nobody else is allowed."

And that wasn’t going to fly with Cook. After all, he hopes to keep laughing at every twist and turn his life takes.

"I think it'll change it in the way that I would always hope growing up with a generation of comedy fans,” he explained. “I was a college kid talking to college-age students. And to grow up with a generation of comedy fans, their kids are now coming to my show. I'm family oriented and to be looking at that with Kelsey and our future and family. It all feels like the right timing."

They’re not the only stars who’ve been candid about their age-gap romance. Keep reading for more…

The practice of ignoring what people say about their 32-year age gap is nothing new for the actresses."If someone wants to spend any time thinking I'm strange for loving the most spectacular person on the planet, then that's their problem," Sarah told Modern Luxury in 2018 while discussing her relationship with Holland. "I'm doing just fine."

As for the former Project Runway host, she simply says auf wiedersehen to any negative comments about her 16-year age gap with the Tokio Hotel guitarist."My boyfriend is many years younger than me, and lots of people are questioning that and asking about it," she shared with InStyle in 2018. "That's really the only time when age seems to be shoved in my face and I have to give an answer for it. I don't really think about it that much otherwise."And Heidi—who married Tom the following year—made it clear she's going to continue living life on her terms."You have to just live a happy life without worrying too much about what people think," the supermodel continued, "because worrying is only going to give you more wrinkles."

Meanwhile, the Quantico star has called out a double standard.While she noted people have a lot to say about her being 10 years old than the Jonas Brother singer, she suggested this wouldn't be the case if it were the other way around."People gave us a lot of s--t about that and still do," Priyanka told InStyle. "I find it really amazing when you flip it and the guy is older, no one cares and actually people like it."

Sam Taylor-Johnson & Aaron Taylor-Johnson

And if you'd ask the Fifty Shades of Grey director, she'd say her 23-year age difference with the Kraven the Hunter actor just doesn't come up in their day-to-day.“No, it never does," she said in a 2024 interview with The Guardian. "I mean, it’s coming up now because you’re asking. And it comes up on the outside perspective of people who don’t know us, because I guess people will always...We’re a bit of an anomaly, but it’s that thing: After 14 years you just think, surely by now it doesn’t really matter?”Sam even pointed out her relationship with Aaron has lasted longer than her marriage to her ex-husband Jay Jopling, who is about four years older than she is."So, if you think of it in that way," she continued, "then the age gap doesn’t really make any difference.”

Though the couple share a birthday (Sept. 25), they aren't on the same page...of the calendar."My husband is 25 years older than me; that’s not a secret," the Chicago star told WSJ. Magazine in 2021. "With any relationship, it wouldn’t be normal if there weren’t any ups and downs. The constant is love and respect."

The Parent Trap alum may argue that the only ones who should be focused on his relationship with the Bonniedale Films cofounder is them. T-H-E-M, them. Get the picture?Still, Dennis indicated he and Laura are unfazed by any attention around her being 39 years younger. "We just don't even notice it," he told Today in 2021 about their age difference. "We've never related to someone in my life better than we do. We have such a great relationship. And love finds a way, wherever it is. And you never know, when love is coming, who that's going to be. And you have no control over it. And we just couldn't be happier."

The yoga instructor has admitted she used to judge couples with big age gaps before her relationship with the actor, who is 26 years her senior."Alec and I are on all the lists of 'Celebrities with the Biggest Age Differences' and stuff like that," she explained on her podcast Witches Anonymous in 2022. "And I would look at it and be like, 'This older man wants some young bimbo with no opinions whatsoever. And then that younger woman is obviously a gold digger, and she obviously doesn't even care and is just like OK, whatever, I hope you die and I'm gonna take all your money.'"However, she's since had a change of heart."Now that I'm in that relationship and people will say those things about me regularly, I'm like, 'Oh my God, why was this trained into my head? Why was I so judgmental about other people who are literally just finding love?'" she added. "And maybe their love looks different from you, and from your love, or from what I thought love would be, but it doesn't make it not valid."

Gird your loins because The Devil Wears Prada actor previously spoke about how he almost ended his relationship with the literary agent in the early days of their romance."I'm 21 years older than she is and I didn't want to feel old for the rest of my life!" Stanley told BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs in 2023. "But I knew that this was an incredibly special person.”

The Alfie actress and the Lift actor know not everyone understands their relationship. “I would imagine it would be complicated for anyone to get their head around," Oli put it to Vogue while referencing their 15-year age gap, "but there’s been nothing but love and joy.” And frankly, Sienna suggested nobody else needs to understand it.“I don’t think you can legislate on matters of the heart," she added. "I certainly have never been able to."

The Jurassic Park star recalled a lighthearted moment with his Olympian wife, who is 30 years his junior."I said, 'Which Beatle would I be if I was one of the Beatles?'" he remembered on The Hoda Show. "She said, 'Rex Harrison.' I said, 'Wait a minute, I know we saw that My Fair Lady yesterday. I think you're thinking of that.'"However, Jeff noted it didn't take Emilie long to realize she meant George Harrison. "So there's that kind of thing," he noted of the couple's age gap. But other than their differing cultural touchpoints, he continued, life together is "so far so good."

Rosie Huntington-Whiteley & Jason Statham

The model also doesn't feel the need to deliver a fast and furious response to any critics of her 20-year age gap with the actor."His knowledge and strength are really inspiring and attractive, and that can come with a man who's had a bit of time," she told Glamour in 2013. "We have a connection that has nothing to do with age. Work comes and goes, but if you have someone at home who thinks you're the greatest person in the world, that keeps you going."

As for how the American Idol alum feels about any judgment towards her nearly 35-year age gap with the composer? Probably so over it."I totally get the judgment initially, but things are never as they appear," Katharine said on Dr. Berlin's Informed Pregnancy Podcast in 2023. "And I'm in love with our love story, and that's all that matters is that I'm in love with the love story."

One thing that’s not unwritten? The way Kristin felt about her 13-year age gap with ex-boyfriend Mark Estes. “Me dating a 24-year-old is not something that I was searching out,” The Hills alum said on a March 2024 episode of her podcast Let’s Be Honest. “It’s not something that I ever thought would ever happen. If you guys listen to the podcast, you know I thought 30-year-olds were too young for me.” And while Kristin said she understands how “it looks to the outside world,” she insisted Mark is “not a typical 24-year-old” and that there’s more to a person than their birth year. “I really think age is just a number,” she continued. “It’s what you’ve been through in your life, how you were raised. There are just so many factors that go into maturity other than age.”But months later, Kristin shared she broke up with Mark.

“I just know long-term he needs to experience life,” she said on an October episode of her podcast. “He’s young. He is. I started to feel the age a bit just with life experience. I look back when I was 24 and how much life has happened for me in between then. Those are crucial years. Those are formative years. This is when you find yourself and he needs to be able to do that.”Still, she called their romance "the best relationship" of her life and expressed hope that Mark will realize their split was for the best."I know that one day he will look back and he will understand it," she added, "and I actually think one day he will thank me."

When the Oscar winner first started crushing on the barrister, he wasn't sure she'd feel the same way.“I liked her, but I didn’t want to jump the shark on it,” George said on The Howard Stern Show about his early romance with Amal. “I couldn’t tell if she liked me. ‘Cause I’m 17 years older than her so she might’ve thought I was grandpa.”However, it turns out she liked him right back and they wed in 2014.

Age is only a number for the Bachelor alum, who is 18 years older than his wife. As he put it during a March 2025 episode of his The Viall Files podcast, "When it comes to age gaps, looks matter."

#705. Yoro red card overturned, but refs' chief Webb backs decision

Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.

"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."

The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb said Barrott got it right.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," he said.

'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?

How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."

Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.

You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.

The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.

A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.

A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.

It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.

Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.

And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.

Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.

This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.

Two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.

Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.

Let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.

Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.

An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.

Make it make sense, supporters might ask.

This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.

Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?

Football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.

Sporting coach Paulo Fonseca speaks to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Manchester United

United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).

The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.

But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".

"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.

"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.

"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."

United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.

Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.

"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.

"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

#704. See Kristen Stewart’s Out of This World Transformation into Sally Ride

Kristen Stewart looked straight out of the 1980s as she transformed into famed NASA astronaut Sally Ride on the set of the upcoming limited series The Challenger.

Where the hell has Kristen Stewart been, loca?

Well, in short, outer space. For the Twilight actress’ latest role as groundbreaking NASA astronaut Sally Ride—a.k.a. the first American woman to fly in space—in The Challenger, she fully changed up her look, rocking a look straight out of the ‘80s.

Stewart donned a brunette bob on the Georgia set of the Prime Video limited series Nov. 24, completing her look with a 1980s style shirt—tied with a bow at the collar—and a dark pair of bottoms. The 36-year-old kept warm on set with a fluffy zip-up sweater as she sipped on a Diet Coke between takes.

The role marks the Oscar nominee’s first regular TV role, with her also serving as a producer on the series alongside wife Dylan Meyers through their production company Nevermind Pictures.

And for Stewart, she couldn’t believe she had the chance to bring Ride’s story to life.

“I’m shaking in boots, but I get to play Sally Ride,” she shared with Collider in December. “The story is incredible and the team is just so inspired and trustworthy and I think I'm in the safest hands.”

The limited series is inspired by Meredith E. Bagby’s 2023 book The New Guys, which chronicled the story of Ride and her fellow astronauts who all broke barriers as NASA’s 1978 astronaut class.

In addition to being the first American woman—and third woman—to fly in space in 1983, Ride also served on the committees that investigated the explosions of the Space Shuttle Challenger in 1986 and the Space Shuttle Columbia in 2003, making her the only person to participate in both.

While she was married to fellow astronaut Steven Hawley from 1982 to 1987, Ride was in a long term relationship with women’s tennis star Tam O’Shaughnessy from 1985 until her death in 2012 from pancreatic cancer at the age of 61. However, Ride hid the fact that she was part of the LGBTQ community during her lifetime, with the news only coming out when O’Shaughnessy was noted to have been her partner of 27 years in her obituary.

Following her death, O’Shaughnessy spoke about the couple’s time together, sharing that while Ride never officially came out to her family, they were all still very accepting of the couple’s relationship.

“Sally never verbally, openly told her mother, her father, or her sister, Bear, that she was gay and that we were a couple. But Sally never hid it from them,” she explained to the Windy City Times in 2013, “you know, I went everywhere with Sally, and she went everywhere with me.”

“Her parents are really smart—especially her mother and her sister,” the former tennis pro added, “they knew a long time ago that we were a couple.”

#703. Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s new biology skills wow scientists

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0)

Earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology company called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

And on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed new proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

The research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” says Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

But some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

The release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 launched a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing new proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI

To see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

In other experiments, the OpenAI team showed that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

Jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, believes that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in even each capability,” he says.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03836-z

#702. Dead hippo to be honoured on football club tifo

Fiona first rose to fame when she was born premature at Cincinnati Zoo in 2017

Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.

Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 2017, died on Thursday after swallowing a woollen hat that had slipped into her enclosure.

The Ohio side will now raise a banner depicting the nine-year-old semi-aquatic mammal in their post-season MLS Cup encounter with Nashville, who won the Supporters' Shield for being the highest-placed team in the league campaign.

Cincinnati said Fiona was a "beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world".

The tifo will be produced by fan group The Forge Cincy, who painted the display on Sunday in a garage next to Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.

The club will also make a donation in Fiona's memory for every fan in attendance to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden.

Fan group The Forge Cincy had previously spent two weeks creating a tifo for their "Hell is Real" October derby match against Ohio rivals Columbus

Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says

Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

Cincinnati's Nick Hagglund, who hails from the city and is in his eighth season with the team, previously paid tribute to Fiona after scoring in his side's 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day of her death.

The defender yelled "that's for Fiona", mimicking the ears on top of her head, in a celebration video, external on the club's Instagram.

Later, on his Instagram account, external, Hagglund posted, "This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.

"Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call."

Cincinnati's tifo is one of a number of tributes paid to the hippo, with Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins wearing a Fiona sweater, external prior to his American football franchise's defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday.

Meanwhile handlers of the blue hippo balloon at New York's annual Macy's Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.

At birth, Fiona weighed 13kg (29lb), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species, and she previously inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

From premature baby to social media star - famed Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies

Fiona swallowed the woollen hat around 10 days prior to her death, with the item getting into her enclosure by accident after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.

Hippos normally live up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.

Nashville finished top of the MLS Eastern Conference, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati.

However, having beaten Orlando in a one-off wildcard round, Cincinnati defeated Nashville 1-0 in the opening match of their best-of-three round one series.

Should Cincinnati win on Saturday they will progress to a one-off conference semi-final with either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC, with a conference final prior to the season-ending MLS Cup final.

#701. Palace docked points for using four sub windows in WSL win

Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.

Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.

However, manager Jo Potter brought on Kirsty Howat for Shannon O'Brien in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to try and shore up the victory.

It was the fourth separate substitution made by Potter, who had also made changes in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time wasting.

Crystal Palace deducted points following WSL win

Palace have been stripped of the three points they earned in the match - one of only two WSL games the Eagles have won this season.

This punishment drops Palace down one place in the WSL table to 13th - the relegation play-off place.

Palace are now below fellow promoted side Birmingham City in the table on goal difference, with both sides now having six points - six behind Everton in 11th.

In a statement on their club website, external Palace said they were "disappointed" by the decision.

The decision was made by an independent tribunal after Palace admitted the breach of competition rule 5.19.1.

The rule states: "A substitution can only be made when play is stopped for any reason and the referee has given permission. A club at its discretion may use five substitute players during a match. For the avoidance of doubt, each club has no more than three substitution opportunities in each match."

The tribunal said that while the rule breach was inadvertent and "not intended to secure an unfair advantage", it said a points deduction was necessary in order to provide a deterrent to clubs against making a similar mistake in future.

"The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained, save in exceptional circumstances," the tribunal stated in its full written decision., external

They said the lateness of the substitution in the match - so late that Howat did not touch the ball after coming on - did not excuse Palace from punishment.

It also ruled "that responsibility for complying with the rule rests with clubs, not match officials".

Palace - who placed the word "fourth" in inverted commas in their response to the ruling - are aiming to improve on their only previous WSL campaign in 2024-25, where they only won twice in 22 matches and were relegated by a 10-point margin.

Their statement read: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty â a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."

Forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith had scored the only goal of the game in the 34th minute on her Palace debut.

#700. Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay

The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.

The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.

The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.

It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.

The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.

As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.

He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.

Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup."

Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

His parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.

Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.

After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.

#698. 90 Day Fiancé Alum Sheila Mangubat's Cause of Death Revealed

After 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days alum Sheila Mangubat died at age 35, sign language interpreter Aimee Adiwang, who worked with the couple, shared her cause of death.

New details about Sheila Mangubat's private health battle have come to light.

After the 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days alum's former fiancé David Dangerfield confirmed she had died at 35, the cause has been revealed.

Mangubat and Dangerfield's sign language interpreter Aimee Adiwang shared with Page Six in a Nov. 24 statement that the reality star died suddenly after a battle with a gynecological cancer at age 35 in the Philippines.

Adiwang—who worked with the pair since Dangerfield was born deaf and used sign language to communicate—did not specify the cancer she was diagnosed with. Mangubat's niece had also told her that her aunt had suffered from a urinary tract infection (UTI) prior to her death.

The interpreter reflected on their time working together during season six of the 90 Day spinoff in an emotional Instagram tribute alongside screengrabs from the 2023 episode.

Even though these are one of the few photos we have together," Adiwang wrote on Instagram Nov. 23. "I'm holding onto them tightly as I remember where our friendship began. Honoring her life and the warmth she brought into mine as she rests peacefully with the Lord."

She concluded, "I will always be grateful for her presence in my life."

Dangerfield initially shared the news in an emotional Instagram message Nov. 22, noting that the family of Mangubat—whom he split from in October 2025 due to distance and K-1 visa issues, but eventually began dating again in June, according to TMZ—told him about her death.

"I am devastated and still trying to process this loss," he continued. "Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support."

Although their romance had its ups and downs, the 45-year-old only had love for Mangubat, who leaves behind son Jhonreil from a previous relationship.

"I'm happy I never gave up because I found my love," he said on a June 2023 episode. "I have a girlfriend whose name is Sheila, and she's beautiful."

"When I first saw Sheila's picture, it got my heart beating," he continued. "I will have a new family with Sheila in the future. Sheila is better than any other woman I've dated because Sheila is a sweet person. She is the perfect match to me. I'll love Sheila forever."

#697. Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Ties Hot Country Songs Record With 50 Weeks at No. 1

The hit matches Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line's "Meant To Be."

Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” logs a 50th week atop Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart (dated Nov. 28), matching the all-time record set by Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line’s “Meant To Be” in 2017-18.

“Choosin’ Texas” totaled 16.9 million official streams, 45.5 million in airplay audience and 6,000 sales in the United States Nov. 13-19, according to Luminate.

The song also extends its Billboard Hot 100 record to 29 weeks at No. 1.

Here’s a rundown of the five longest-leading Hot Country Songs hits (since the list became the genre’s singular songs chart in October 1958):

“Meant To Be” debuted atop Hot Country Songs in December 2017 and held the summit for 50 consecutive weeks. “Choosin’ Texas” reached No. 1 in its sixth week, in February, and led for 28 frames before Taylor Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” interrupted its reign for two weeks in June. Langley reclaimed the summit on the July 4 chart and has remained there for 22 more weeks in a row.

The shared milestone also links two distinct moments in country’s crossover history. “Meant To Be” emerged during a sonically experimental boom, pairing pop star Rexha with FGL, a country cornerstone act in the 2010s, as genre-blurring hits helped define the era. The collaboration reached No. 2 on the Hot 100.

“Choosin’ Texas,” meanwhile, has contributed to country’s prominence this decade.

Streaming and radio airplay at country, pop and adult formats helped sustain both hits’ extraordinary longevity. “Meant To Be” spent 55 weeks atop Country Streaming Songs, with “Choosin’ Texas” up to 44. Their commands on Country Airplay were one and three weeks, respectively (reflecting radio’s more focused programming cycles).

Both songs also hit the top 10 on Pop Airplay, Adult Pop Airplay and Adult Contemporary, and sold strongly. “Meant To Be” reached No. 2 on Digital Song Sales over a yearlong stay on the chart; “Choosin’ Texas” has led for a record 22 weeks and counting.

Check Billboard.com next Monday, Nov. 30, to find out if “Choosin’ Texas” can pass “Meant To Be” and give Langley sole possession of the Hot Country Songs No. 1 longevity record.

#696. Bayern hold 'constructive' talks over Musiala's health

Jamal Musiala has started one Bundesliga game this season

Bayern Munich are only focused on getting Jamal Musiala back from injury and are not interested in the comments made regarding his contract, the club's sporting director Max Eberl insisted.

The 23-year-old collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Last week, players' union Fifpro said Bayern Munich's hierarchy "should know better" after the club's honorary president Uli Hoeness said the midfielder may never "regain the performance level he once had".

Describing the talks on Tuesday as "very, very constructive", Eberl said the focus was on Musiala's recovery from a recent injury.

"Today it was about just how we want to get Jamal back on the field, just like before his muscle injury in the international break," Eberl said.

"That's the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something."

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen questioned the lucrative contract extension the Germany international signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal, external may need to be renegotiated.

Bayern manager Vincent Kompany said in September it wouldn't be "a big deal" if the seizures return.

Musiala, previously a regular starter and one of the best young talents in Europe, has played five times this season, scoring twice.

"Contracts are there to be respected," Fifpro said on Saturday. "An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."

#695. Looking Ahead: A Release Calendar of Upcoming Albums in 2026

We'll be updating our list as musicians announce their new music, so keep checking back for the latest!

Keeping track of all the upcoming releases from favorite artists can sometimes be a bit of a challenge. It’s not unusual for musicians to tease an album, then reveal a release date, only for the LP to be delayed for one reason or another (in some cases, multiple times), often without a new release date attached. Then there are albums that are announced mere days before they drop!

But we’ve got you! Musicians from across genres started teasing new projects and announcing album release dates for the new year as it barely started. And like the last several trips around the sun, we’re keeping a calendar to keep track of all the notable releases of the year.

One of the most highly anticipated releases was Hilary Duff’s Luck…or Something — her first album in 10 years — which dropped in February. The singer-actress first announced her return to music in September, when she revealed a new label deal with Atlantic Records, as well as new music and a docuseries that will follow her musical comeback.

BTS also gave its ARMY news to celebrate just days after the new year kicked off. On Jan. 4, the K-pop supergroup revealed that its highly anticipated next album — which comes after the members took a yearslong break as a group to complete mandatory duties for the South Korean military and focus on solo ventures — would arrive in March.

Not to be outdone, fellow K-pop supergroup BLACKPINK also announced its own new music in early January, with DEADLINE dropping in February. (Then in August, three of the ladies announced solo projects to arrive this year!)

Harry Styles then followed up BLACKPINK’s announcement the next day with his own album reveal. The pop superstar’s fourth studio album made its debut in March.

As winter moved into spring, women superstars not only teased, but announced highly anticipated albums. Among them? Madonna, Olivia Rodrigo and Ariana Grande, with all three projects arriving before the end of July.

As September rolled around, some big names in rock released their projects. Among them are Anthrax and Rage Against the Machine’s Tom Morello, while October will anticipate an album by Nickelback, as well as iconic industrial band Ministry, who returns with its final album. And before the end of the month, Miley Cyrus returned with Bass Persuades.

But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Taylor Swift revealed on Sept. 22 that she had a new song titled “Patient Zero” coming before the end of the month. Less than 24 hours later, she surprised Swifties with the news that not only was there a new track coming, but The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, featuring not just one new song, but four.

As fall swept in with a chill, the anticipation was hot … for Grand Theft Auto 6. The highly anticipated video game announced that there would be two music releases: a soundtrack featuring the likes of Cardi B, Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Rauw Alejandro, Morgan Wallen and more. On top of that, Justice had helmed the score. Both would arrive before year’s end.

That’s just several of the big releases of 2026. To help you stay on top of it all, we’ve organized this calendar chronologically by month and week, and have also included a section for albums that have been announced, but do not yet have a release date.

Keep checking back for the latest 2026 album release dates!

#694. Millwall face partial stadium closure after discriminatory chants

Millwall, who are 16th in the Championship, have average league gates of 19,418 at The Den this season

Millwall have been ordered to play a future Championship match in front of a partially-closed stadium as punishment for fans' discriminatory chants.

The club has also been fined Â£70,000 by an independent regulatory commission, and been told another offence this season will lead to a further partial stadium closure.

The sanctions were imposed for ableist and homophobic chants, heard at a game against Charlton Athletic in January.

"These chants are discriminatory, unacceptable, and will not be tolerated at The Den or anywhere Millwall play," Millwall's managing director Mark Fairbrother said in an open letter to supporters., external

"The club condemns them without reservation. They do not represent this club, and the vast majority of supporters who follow Millwall home and away with passion and pride.

"Incidents like this hurt all of us, but none more so than people who are directly discriminated against by ableist, homophobic or other unacceptable chanting, and we apologise to anybody that was affected, offended or impacted by the chants."

Blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 of the Dockers Stand - the two-tiered east stand at The Den - will have to be closed for the Championship fixture against Sheffield United on 8 December.

It is the first time a club has been given this level of sanction for discriminatory chanting, with the commission saying "the club's previous disciplinary record was a significant aggravating feature".

The commission pointed to chants relating to race in a 2019 fixture against Everton, religion in a 2023 fixture away at Wigan Athletic, and sexual orientation and disability in a 2025 visit to Crystal Palace, all of which resulted in fines for the club.

"History has shown that combinations of action plans and fines have been wholly ineffective to prevent the club - through its supporters - committing breaches" of Football Association (FA) rules around discriminatory behaviour, the commission added.

The FA had charged Millwall in March for the chanting against Charlton.

The club admitted the charge, and in its submissions suggested the chants were limited to 80 to 100 individuals in the north-eastern corner of the Dockers Stand, in the blocks that will be closed as part of the punishment.

However, based on other evidence, the commission concluded the actual figure involved in the chants was "likely to have been in the hundreds, quite possibly more".

It also found that the club did not make any announcement over the stadium PA system ordering for the discriminatory chanting to stop, nor did it deploy any additional stewards or police to the areas from where the chanting was originating.

"I won't dress this up. This is a serious outcome," Fairbrother said.

"This significant sanction was given because, although this is the first charge relating to a match at The Den for many years, the commission took into account a number of incidents of discriminatory chanting involving our supporters over the past few seasons at away games.

"This is the cumulative cost of that pattern. Most importantly, the current and any future sanctions mean the next incident won't just cost the club money. It will cost supporters their seats.

"Innocent fans will be shut out of their own stadium because of someone else's behaviour, and with future sanctions likely to be tougher, that threat is very real."

#693. Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title

Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

With the game goalless, Senegal left the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. The match in Rabat was delayed by over 15 minutes before Morocco's Brahim Diaz had his spot-kick saved.

Senegal then triumphed 1-0 after extra time, with Pape Gueye scoring the winner.

That result was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed the Teranga Lions had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play after the penalty was awarded.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners.

A statement issued by Cas said the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority".

"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume."

The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa".

"The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later said in a statement.

"This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law."

Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision".

Caf says it respects the Cas award and "will take all the necessary measures to implement it".

The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality.

'Shameful' and 'terrible look' - the chaos that marred Afcon 2025 final

'The longest VAR check in history' - the fallout from shock Afcon decision

Senegal's walk-off during the final in Rabat has already brought about a change in football's rules.

"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at â a âreferee's decision," said Ifab, the game's lawmaking body, in April.

"This new rule will also apply âto any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match âto be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match."

Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the Afcon 2025 final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining.

Referee Ndala was at the centre of the controversy during the Afcon final

A tightly contested final between the continent's top-ranked sides produced two moments of controversy in second-half stoppage time, with referee Ndala at the centre of the drama.

First the Congolese official denied Senegal a near-certain goal, blowing his whistle for a challenge by Abdoulaye Seck on Morocco right-back Achraf Hakimi moments before Ismaila Sarr nodded in.

The free-kick looked soft, but the video assistant referee (VAR) was unable to get involved because Ndala had awarded the foul before the ball crossed the line.

Three minutes later came a flashpoint in the Senegal box, when El Hadji Malick Diouf tugged Morocco playmaker Diaz back before heading a corner clear.

Diaz vehemently claimed a penalty and Ndala eventually awarded a spot-kick after being sent to consult his pitchside monitor by the VAR.

Senegal coach Pape Thiaw called his players over to the touchline, and Thiaw subsequently headed down the tunnel to the changing room in protest against the decision - accompanied by several players.

They eventually returned, but over 15 minutes had elapsed since the award of the penalty by the time Real Madrid's Diaz failed to convert, with his Panenka-style attempt easily saved by goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.

Meanwhile, there was unrest inside the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium as a small contingent of Senegal supporters clashed with security staff.

The game went into extra time, with midfielder Gueye scoring the goal which settled the contest in Senegal's favour.

Off the pitch, another match involving disciplinary boards and lawyers would soon begin.

Brahim Diaz's penalty was saved by Edouard Mendy after Senegal's walk-off led to a delay of over 15 minutes before he was able to take the spot-kick

Senegal celebrated their second continental title but the FRMF quickly lodged an appeal with Caf, arguing their opponents had breached Article 82 of Afcon regulations, which covers withdrawals.

It states that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" it shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

A disciplinary board from the continental game's governing body rejected the FRMF's appeal days after the final as it sanctioned and fined those found guilty of unsporting conduct during the match.

Yet in March, almost two months on from the final, a Caf appeals board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The FSF described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and swiftly lodged its case with Cas.

The director general of the Switzerland-based court said arbitration proceedings would be conducted "as swiftly as possible", but it was over five months until all parties descended on Lausanne for a one-day hearing.

The Cas panel was led by Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.

Both the FRMF and FSF were able to nominate an arbitrator to exercise an independent judicial function once their appointment was confirmed.

The FRMF nominated Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli, while the FSF nominated Hamburg-based attorney and professor of âlaw at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas. Those two men completed the Cas panel.

Over six weeks on from that hearing - and 10 months since the Afcon 2025 final - Senegal have been proclaimed champions once again.

But the debate and damage done to the reputation of African football is likely to linger for some time yet.

In its appeal, the FSF argued that the decision of referee Ndala to resume the match in the 19th minute of added time - and to allow it to be concluded with a sporting result - could not be reviewed, pursuant to the 'field of play' doctrine.

Cas has a long-standing practice where it refrains from "reviewing decisions taken on the playing field by referees for applying the rules of the game, unless there is evidence that those rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith".

The FRMF argued, on the contrary, that the referee's decision did not fall under the field of play doctrine because Senegal should have faced disciplinary consequences for walking off the pitch.

The Moroccan federation went on to argue that, according to Afcon tournament rules, the referee should have brought the match to an early conclusion.

It added that Ndala "erred in law" and that his decision was "arbitrary".

However, in the view of the panel, the referee's decisions were limited to the pitch and the relevant Afcon regulations regarding withdrawals were not applicable.

"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," the Cas statement added.

"However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary'. On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."

Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstates Senegal as Afcon winners

Despite Cas being the highest authority in sport, and its decision coming 10 months on from the final, there could yet be a further twist.

The FRMF raised a grievance with the process before the panel's judgement was announced on Tuesday.

It alleged that German attorney Haas, the arbitrator on the panel nominated by the Senegalese, held a telephone call with FSF president Abdoulaye Fall on Sunday.

Fall "categorically" denies that any such phone call ever took place.

The FRMF says that any unauthorised communication between a member of the panel and one of the interested parties would constitute a serious breach of Cas regulations.

It has demanded that "appropriate legal consequences be applied to actions that compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process".

The Moroccans could appeal against the ruling by taking the case to the Swiss Federal Tribunal, and the country's highest court could set Cas' judgement aside.

The case would then likely be heard again at Cas, with a different panel in place.

A precedent would be the case of Chinese swimmer Sun Yang, who had an appeal against the decision by Cas to impose an eight-year doping ban upheld by the Swiss Federal Tribunal.

A new panel heard his case at Cas, and his ban was reduced to four years and three months.

#692. Britt Stewart's Ultimate Guide to "Thoughtful & Curated" Holiday Gifts

DWTS' Britt Stewart is not only a great dancer, but a very thoughtful holiday gift giver! She exclusively revealed to E! her intentional tricks and gift ideas to help you win the holiday season.

The last thing anyone wants for the holidays is a gift that feels impersonal! To avoid giving something to your loved ones that they'll just toss to the side and not actually appreciate, it's time to get serious with your gift-giving this year.

Ahead of the Dancing With the Stars season 35 finale, E! exclusively chatted with pro Britt Stewart, who is not only a dancer with moves we envy, but a very intentional gift giver:

"I’ll always choose giving an experience over things because creating memories with the people I love most is incredibly important to me," she told us. "If I chose to gift something physical, it has to be thoughtful and curated specifically for the person receiving it. As a self-care advocate, my favorite gifts are the ones that remind people to pause, reset, and take a little time for themselves."

And as for her favorite part of celebrating the holiday season, it's building holiday memories with her husband, actor and her former DWTS partner, Daniel Durant.

"For me, the best part of celebrating the holidays is spending quality time with my family. My husband Daniel and I got married last August and we’re still creating what our own holiday traditions look like, which makes it extra special. I also love that the end of the year gives us all a genuine reason to slow down, be present with the people we love most and reflect on the past year," she shared.

Scroll on for all of Britt's thoughtful gift ideas and tips, including her Los Angeles favorites, just in time for the holidays.

Do you have any current favorites in your beauty routine that you think would make great holiday gifts for beauty lovers?

"My favorite beauty tool right now is the Therabody Face depuffing wand, which cools and heats, and is one of my favorite things to do during my morning rituals. I put on a daily sheet mask and use the cool setting first to help my face depuff, then switch to the heated setting to help the serum really penetrate my skin. It is a must have and would make an amazing gift for the beauty and skin care enthusiasts in your life."

This celeb-loved depuffing tool has cold and heat treatments to help reduce under-eye puffiness, enhance radiance and diminish the look of dark circles.

What’s a gift you’ve received that you get so much use out of?

"One of the best parts about gift-giving is getting someone something they wouldn’t normally buy for themselves, but actually really need. My husband Daniel is always up to date on the latest technology, so last year he gifted me a new laptop. It was something I hadn’t done for myself in over ten years, and it’s a gift that I use on a daily basis!"

Lightweight and portable, this MacBook is available in four different colors, each with a vibrant 13-inch display.

"Not every gift needs to be as big as a new laptop and sometimes gifts that are inspired by a conversation with a friend mean so much! You spend a lot of time on the road for DWTS tour - what are some must-haves you always bring that a travel lover might appreciate for a holiday gift?

"A must-have for traveling are my packing cubes. I love to stay organized and I have a place for almost everything, so packing cubes for your clothes and a nice travel toiletry bag are always the way to go for anyone who travels a lot."

#691. Nick Carter Ordered to Stand Trial on Sexual Assault Claims From Dream Singer Melissa Schuman

The Backstreet Boys member denies assaulting Schuman or any of the other women who've accused him of sexual misconduct.

A judge has decided to hold a trial in the sexual assault lawsuit brought against Backstreet Boys member Nick Carter by Melissa Schuman, a former member of the teen-pop group Dream.

A Monday (Nov. 23) court ruling, obtained by Billboard, says there “is a triable issue of material fact” as to whether Carter forced Schuman to have sex when they were co-starring in the teen horror movie The Hollow in 2003. A trial is set for May 2027 in Santa Monica, Calif.

Schuman sued Carter in 2023 under California’s Sexual Abuse and Cover-Up Accountability Act, a state law that temporarily lifted the statute of limitations for otherwise-expired sex assault claims. Under that law, claims only qualified for revival if there was an allegation that some business entity had conspired to “cover up” a prior sexual assault by the same perpetrator.

Carter vehemently denies Schuman’s sexual battery claim and has countersued her, as well as various other sexual assault accusers, for defamation. His lawyers argued that Schuman’s case had a fatal defect: she failed to allege the right kind of cover-up, meaning it was not eligible for California’s 2023 claim revival window.

However, California passed another law last year, called the Justice for Survivors of Sexual Assault Act, that opened another two-year window for sexual assault claims with looser cover-up requirements. Judge Lisa K. Sepe-Wiesenfeld ruled Monday that this second law can be successfully used to revive Schuman’s claims.

“The individual claim against defendant Carter for sexual battery is proper irrespective of the existence of a cover up,” wrote the judge. “Defendants cannot prevail on summary adjudication merely by attacking the cover-up allegations.”

The question at this stage, then, is merely whether there’s enough conflicting evidence in the case to go to a jury. Judge Sepe-Wiesenfeld believes the answer is yes, since Schuman has said that Carter assaulted her, while the singer said it never happened.

“There is a conflict in the evidence presented as to whether a sexual assault of Plaintiff occurred,” wrote the judge.

A lawyer for Schuman, Jamie Majerus, tells Billboard that Monday’s ruling “reflects the existence of substantial factual disputes that must be resolved by a jury.”

“Among the evidence before the Court is sworn testimony from Carter’s own sister, who testified he had sex with a 15-year-old, and testimony from his best friend at the time, describing repeated episodes of extreme alcohol consumption, including drinking an entire bottle of tequila at a time and forcing himself to vomit afterward,” said Majerus. “A jury, not the defense, will decide what weight to give that evidence.”

Carter’s lawyers did not immediately return a request for comment on Tuesday (Nov. 24).

The Backstreet Boys member has faced various public accusations of sexual assault over the last decade, all of which he denies. He’s been sued by three other women in addition to Schuman: Shannon Ruth, Ashley Repp and Laura Penly. Carter is currently scheduled to go to trial on those claims next August in Las Vegas.

#690. Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro (second left) is shown a red card by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.

"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.

"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.

"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"

United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.

They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.

It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.

Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.

There has been no apology from Webb on this occasion.

Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball."

United sources claim this interpretation is wrong.

The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.

This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.

Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.

"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.

"We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?"

What referee's chief Webb said about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.

"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.

"That if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong."
