#674. Every Track From ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Ranked — Now Including the Deluxe Bonus Tracks

GTA's accompanying soundtrack arrived 24 hours after the long-anticipated Rockstar video game — and they didn't waste time releasing the deluxe edition days later.

Monocultural moments in society have become extremely rare in the mid-2020s, but the arrival of Grand Theft Auto VI has brought about as strong a unified pop-culture tidal wave as we’ve seen this decade.

Rockstar Games released the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album on Friday (Nov. 20) through Atlantic Records as an accompanying soundtrack to the long-awaited video game, which arrived 24 hours earlier.

As Billboard details in our latest cover story about the songs, score and soundtrack of GTA VI, Rockstar didn’t spare any expense when plotting the music for the immersive game. The original 34-song soundtrack features Playboi Carti, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Lana Del Rey, Gunna, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Yung Lean, Future, Metro Boomin, Travis Scott, Fred again.., PinkPantheress, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala, Fuerza Regida and more.

GTA VI will look to make even more history with a No. 1 debut on the charts — as no video game soundtrack has topped the Billboard 200 before.

Artist-hosted radio stations dominate the Vice City airwaves, with stations helmed or curated by the likes of Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, Trina and Trick Daddy, PinkPantheress, Burna Boy and Robyn.

The Grand Theft Auto VI festivities will continue into the weekend, with a music festival at Miami’s Mana Wynwood on Nov. 21. The festival is set to have Cardi B, Travis Scott, Rauw Alejandro and more hit the stage, including a Cactus Jack ensemble featuring Scott, Don Toliver, SoFaygo and a cameo from Florida’s own Kodak Black.

After GTA hit pop culture with a tsunami takeover, Rockstar Games and Atlantic Records continued to flood the marketplace with a 23-track deluxe edition of the album, which arrived on Monday (Nov. 23). They didn’t stop there, as an iTunes exclusive four-pack was released on Tuesday (Nov. 24) to ensure the full-court press.

Take a break from perusing Leonida with Jason and Lucia and find all of the tracks from the Grand Theft Auto: The Album along with the new deluxe edition (sans the five Overmono songs that feel more like a score) and iTunes exclusives ranked in order below.

Who knew Omar Apollo had a funky little party-starter like this up his sleeve? Drawing on the iconic Stalag riddim immortalized by Sister Nancy’s “Bam Bam,” “No Me Busques” bursts with a wailing chorus with an infectious call-and-response hook. Oh, and that festive saxophone riff. Lyrically, there’s not much to it beyond Apollo’s repeated insistence that someone stop looking for him. The groove does most of the talking. — ISABELA RAYGOZA

This track is a little different from what I’m used to, but I like it. It plays during the opening credits of GTA VI and serves as the opening track on the game’s album. Sonically, it has a heavy ’80s-inspired synth pulse, electro-disco drums and electric piano that make me feel like it could fit perfectly into any season of Stranger Things.

It’s the perfect way to open the game’s soundtrack. The song is about starting from zero and hustling your way toward success, which feels right at home in the world of GTA. It sets the tone for the kind of journey players are about to embark on. — CHRISTOPHER CLAXTON

Joe Armon-Jones is here to lower your cortisol levels while strolling around Leonida, listening to the luscious instrumentation of “Hotel Alphonso.” — M.S.

Sak pase? Kodak Black teams up with DJ Michael Brun and the duo connects with their Haitian roots, as Yak mixes in Haitian Creole while playfully roasting someone’s baldy haircut and rapping about flipping cocaine. — M.S.

GTA is supposed to have something for everyone, and the metalheads make their presence felt with the thrash aggression of Power Trip’s “Mutual Death Warrant.” I’m ready to either run through a wall or fire up Guitar Hero after pressing play thanks to the Dallas band. — M.S.

The Dare’s synth-heavy brand of dance-punk has invaded the mainstream thanks to pop stars like Charli xcx and ADÉLA leaning into and elevating the subgenre. He serves up the robotic “Interesting” here, which will spin on the EDM radio stations around Leonida and get The Dare a set at Space replica The Vault in Vice City. — M.S.

Separate from his nu-disco Holy Ghost! running mate Nick Millhiser, Alex Frankel wants you to dance in Leonida with the groovy “Playa Rosa,” which is perfect for a top-down cruise down the coastline or a night at The Vault. — M.S.

This is an interesting track and an unapologetically raunchy celebration of sexual confidence, which is exactly the kind of energy we can expect from Sexyy Red. Real Dimez and Sexyy lean into their provocative personalities for a playful record that doesn’t take itself too seriously. Even the title “Cooties” plays on the childhood idea that girls have cooties and that boys stay away from them because they’re afraid of infection. Now, the tables have turned and these ladies are having fun with the concept. — C.C.

A dance-house track that makes it clear this duo doesn’t play around — and that anyone can catch a beatdown. — C.C.

Primal percussion, glitchy electronics and unbridled sexual energy collide on Arca’s self-produced “Sandunguea.” The Venezuelan experimentalist delivers a delirious invitation to dance and indulge, peppering her verses with colorful slang from her homeland. Against abrasive beats, her vocals switch between flirtation and feverish demands, breathy moans and fragmented chants. “Nuestra pasarela es la calle” (the street is our runway), she declares. In true Arca fashion, the dance floor becomes a space for uninhibited self-expression, where pleasure and chaos go hand in hand. — I.R.

“All Again” is about missing someone after a relationship has ended, and wondering whether the love, memories and heartbreak were worth it in the end. It captures that feeling of looking back on a relationship and questioning whether you’d put yourself through it all over again. I’m not sure I would. Would you? — C.C.

After closing out Grand Theft Auto V with the final credits track “The Setup,” Favored Nations returns to push the tempo on the sixth installment’s iTunes-exclusive foursome with the blissful “There Is Only Us.” — M.S.

Rina Sawayama made waves with her assist on Charli xcx’s “Beg for You” in 2022, and the Japanese pop artist/model is back in the mainstream with the brooding “TRDWFE.” I’m going to be hearing Sawayama asking us to “submit” repeatedly when my head hits the pillow tonight — although “TRDWFE” sounds like it was tailor-made more for the likes of HBO’s The Idol than the GTA vibe. — MICHAEL SAPONARA

With Travis Scott all over Grand Theft Auto‘s rollout, it’s only right he reserved a slot for one of Cactus Jack’s offspring. Sofaygo makes the most of his appearance on “Cashout,” a syrupy melodic blend that SahBabii would’ve been a perfect running mate for. — M.S.

It’s clear that 21 Savage will stand ten toes down on his reputation, street credibility and distrust of his opps. Throughout the track, he draws a line between people who talk about violence and those who are actually willing to stand on business. Savage doesn’t want listeners to forget that actions speak louder than words, and if you’re not really about it, he has no time to waste on you. Don’t forget, Twitter fingers will get you nowhere. As he puts it, “We get up and go at all the smoke, you n—as go live.” — C.C.

Metro is back on production for this one. It’s a quick track about flexing, so you already know the deal: money, cars, clothes and relationships. Thug keeps it short and straight to the point, delivering the kind of flex-heavy record that fits right into the GTA lifestyle. Just remember, anything born out of a criminal lifestyle comes with real consequences. — C.C.

“You Move Me” was made for a top-down cruise through Leonida. NEIL FRANCES’ blend of disco and EDM gives a callback to 1980s Vice City, but something that still feels like it could exist in the modern dance world. — M.S.

Young Nudy lives at the intersection of gaming and rap, so Nudy making an appearance on the soundtrack shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. He serves up the sinister “Don Da Da,” which finds him as a kingpin calling shots, while the track could’ve been an offshoot that didn’t make the cut from his Just Doin Me project. — M.S.

Fcukers is back. The NYC duo’s first release since Ö comes with the house-leaning “Only One” and they’re here to start the party and blow out your speakers. If there’s a rave somewhere in Leonida, Fcukers is headlining. Can we get Tinashe to sprinkle her Popstar magic on a remix? Vocalist Shanny Wise even moonlights as a co-host of GTA Radio’s Stockyard FM alongside PinkPantheress and The Dare in the video game. — M.S.

All the baddies to the front, please! “GMA” stands for “Get Money Anthem,” because if you can’t make money in GTA, what the hell can you do? Hope y’all caught that reference. This is an upbeat party anthem celebrating women who make their own money, no matter how they earn it. JT isn’t knocking anybody’s hustle, and at this point, neither am I. Whether you’re stacking cash in the game or in real life, the message is to stay focused on your goals and tune out the criticism. Shoutout to all the ladies working traditional 9-to-5s, earning college degrees, dancing or hustling on the side. We see you! — C.C.

Keith Richards puts his own spin on Jimmy Reed’s 1961 blues classic “Bright Lights, Big City” for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album. His version takes a different approach from Reed’s original, but Keith sounds right at home here. It’s a fresh take on a blues classic, and one that fits perfectly into the world of GTA. — C.C.

Fame is a hell of a drug, but Denzel Curry and 454 haven’t forgotten where they came from. “FLA Flow” is a tribute to Florida’s music and hip-hop culture, with both artists reflecting on the street history and neighborhoods that shaped them. — C.C.

The crown jewel of the iTunes exclusive four-pack. 100 gecs wax poetic about their love for marijuana and affinity for getting high on the punk-leaning smoker’s delight “Sensimilla,” while also making time to take shots at Tiger King star Carole Baskin.

With GTA returning to Vice City, having Kodak Black involved was a must. He’s even a character playing himself in the video game’s campaign. A Yak and Don Toliver collaboration seems like an odd pairing on its face — then you mix in the chaotic skittering production, and both the artists and listeners are playing catch-up for the duration of “Let’s Rock.” — M.S.

Opium’s HXG and Tana invite Quavo to their rage rap world with “RCKSTRL!VING” and Huncho makes it work with his trap-laden rhymes mixing in with the grungy soundscape. The rapper-rockstar lifestyle plays an integral role in GTA VI‘s chapter three when the scene switches to downtown Vice City. — M.S.

Offset will always be unapologetic, and “I Just Came To Pop It” is no different. Wealth, status, street credibility and a refusal to back down from anyone are all on display. Offset brags about the lifestyle he’s built, from luxury cars to expensive jewelry, while reflecting on his past in the trap and the life he gets to live today. The contrast between his street beginnings and his multimillion-dollar lifestyle is a reminder of just how far he’s come. You earned it, so pop your s—t, Offset! — C.C.

Tee Grizzley is not one to mess with. “IKYFL” is an unapologetic statement about loyalty, street credibility, success and refusing to let anyone question how far he’s come. The track captures Tee’s mentality of protecting his circle, enjoying the rewards of his success and staying ready for anyone who tries to challenge him. This is one of those tracks that makes you feel untouchable when you’re cruising through Vice City. — C.C.

“Got Dat” debuted on Vice City Rap Radio in GTA VI, and lands on streaming services with the album’s deluxe. Pooh Shiesty’s menacing trap-laden rhymes are a perfect fit for GTA, but, unfortunately, Pooh living out that outlaw lifestyle has landed him behind bars for the foreseeable future. — M.S.

Morgan Wallen colors outside the lines of country while leaning on his pop and R&B influences for “Last Thing You Need.” It’s a smooth, laid-back track for fans to throw on for a late-night cruise through the swamp lands of GTA‘s Leonida. — M.S.

Just when you think you’ve settled into the sleek reggaetón groove of “X,” JHAYCO throws a dance-floor curveball. Co-produced by the Puerto Rican star alongside Tainy and COZY, the track finds Jhay assuring a love interest that he’s nothing like her ex, dishing out a stream of suggestive compliments. But the real thrill comes during the bridge, when bright synths and a pulsating electronic beat give way to a euphoric break before the dembow kicks back in. It’s a catchy little club banger that doubles as a reminder of Jhay’s knack for melding reggaetón with EDM. — I.R.

Of course, the GTA team got the legend Robert Glasper to help close out the album! Bringing together bassist Stanley Clarke, drummer Yussef Dayes and pianist Robert Glasper, this track is straight vibes. No lyrics needed, just let the musicians do their thing. Named after Miami’s historic Overtown neighborhood, the track connects the game’s Vice City map to the real-world roots of Miami. A smooth way to bring the album home. — C.C.

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album wouldn’t be complete without an Afro-fusion track like this. I love the simple, chant-like hook. This might become my new go-to morning affirmation before heading to work or starting a session in GTA. It’s an uplifting song about resilience, bouncing back from setbacks and continuing to reach for greater heights no matter who or what tries to hold you back.

This is the perfect song to play after a mission doesn’t go as planned. Burna is reminding us that no matter the setback or how people treat you, you’re still unstoppable. Nobody is better than you, so keep pushing and get “bigger, bigger, bigger, bigger, hey!” — C.C.

This is baby-making music. Dâm-Funk and The Time’s Jesse Johnson supply the groovy, funky vibes that have been a staple of the GTA series for over two decades. I’m glad the soundtrack composers made room for them here, because Gen Z isn’t going to know what hit them when a new generation of gamers presses play. — M.S.

Grief, trauma and the emotional exhaustion of being unable to escape memories of someone you’ve lost are at the center of HEALTH’s “NIGHTMARE.” The song uses the idea of a nightmare as a metaphor for being trapped in an endless cycle of emotional pain, where the past continues to haunt you. However, by the second half of the track, HEALTH begins shifting toward the idea of waking up, moving forward and learning to separate the past from the present. — C.C.

Tove Lo wasn’t a name I expected to see on the tracklist for GTA VI, but she makes it work and shuts down any detractors who didn’t think she’d belong. “Blood in Your Eyes” is the blaring experimental pop that should be pumping the dance floor at Leonida’s version of the Space and E11EVEN nightclubs in the game. — M.S.

JENNIE is taking another “Power Trip” with this dance-pop track. In JENNIE’s city, there are no limits. This is a celebration of confidence, status and the freedom to do whatever you want without worrying about who approves. She embraces a larger-than-life persona, putting herself at the center of attention while making it clear that she knows her worth. But there’s nothing wrong with a little self-love, so is this really a power trip? — C.C.

If you see Future and Metro Boomin on a track, nine times out of 10, it’s going to be a banger, and this song proves just that. Shoutout to Yung Lean, because I like the track, but I’m not entirely sure if his presence fits. We have Metro handling the production, of course, and Future’s trap-influenced sound just works perfectly over Metro’s production. The two have such a natural chemistry, and this track is another example of why their collaborations rarely miss.– C.C.

Zara Larsson is chasing carefree desire with “Fast Emotion,” and she has no shame about it. She just wants you to “make it reckless, leave [her] breathless, make [her] heart race.” This track is bright, upbeat and full of energy, making it perfect for cruising down Vice City. “Fast Emotion” is all about craving an intense, spontaneous connection and allowing yourself to get swept up in the excitement of the moment. Through imagery of summer nights, physical attraction and speed, Zara captures a romance that feels exhilarating. — C.C.

Outside of Drake, no rapper made more of 2026 than Don Toliver. “TF?” provides the gloomy soundscape where Toliver is at home, compared to “Let’s Rock.” The raunchy tune could’ve been left on the cutting room floor during his OCTANE sessions, but is a worthy addition to the GTA album. — M.S.

A Cherokee loaded with contraband, police sirens blaring and a desperate escape through the city — “Macacoa 2000” opens like a scene straight out of Grand Theft Auto. Over hard-hitting reggaetón produced by Dímelo Ninow, reminiscent of the genre’s gritty 2000s heyday, Rauw Alejandro narrates a chaotic cop chase in a rapid-fire flow. Near the end, the track switches gears into sultrier territory, with the silky R&B vocals that marked his breakthrough. But beneath the bravado is a deeper reverence for reggaetón’s roots. At the beginning, he salutes the genre’s pioneers and reflects on his own longevity: “Se trata de trascender en la música” (It’s about transcending through music). — I.R.

Lana Del Rey shines as Delta Dawne in her role as a co-host of the rebellious Back Country Radio station in GTA. It’s only right she also delivered on the soundtrack, as LDR revels in a tragic romance for her “Crazy for You” ballad. Enter a Jason and Lucia romance scene from the campaign, with Lana providing the accompaniment. — M.S.

“50 Bands” is a braggadocious celebration of money, luxury, sexual confidence and unapologetic competition. The track is packed with personality as Latto and Flo Milli trade witty punchlines back and forth. Both ladies are flexing their looks, money and influence while taking shots at anyone they feel can’t keep up. When Latto and Flo Milli get together, “throw somе racks on it, make it plural.” — C.C.

Fuerza Regida trades corridos for a breezy reggaetón groove on “Suzuki,” a flirtatious, raunchy cut that finds the San Bernardino hitmakers venturing into new territory. Produced by Synthetic, the track glides on glossy electronic textures and a laid-back dembow bounce, while frontman Jesús Ortiz Paz delivers a string of shameless come-ons. From pole dancing and risqué fantasies to a cheeky reference to tusi (a.k.a. pink cocaine), the lyrics leave little to the imagination. The beat may be easygoing, but JOP clearly has no intention of behaving himself. — I.R.

“Aprovecha que tienes mi atención!” Anitta brings “Touch & Go” to life with this English- and Spanish-language version of “Vai Dar Caô,” originally featuring Ebony and Papatinho. Unfortunately, this version is missing those features — but Anitta still delivers the energy when it comes to casual attraction, sexual freedom and knowing how to leave someone wanting more.

On “Touch & Go,” Anitta enjoys the physical chemistry of a relationship, but has no interest in turning it into a deeper emotional commitment. And that sounds like a lot of y’all reading this! You get close, enjoy the moment and move on before the other person starts expecting anything more. A hot, flirtatious atmosphere can be fun for a while, but there’s no shame in wanting something more serious either. — C.C.

If half of Camila Cabello’s heart is in Havana, the other half lies in Miami. The dulcet “Sweet Like Candy” is a solid effort from CC — and like a good piece of candy, it’s not too heavy or sour, as the Fifth Harmony solo star sticks the landing with a fun, surface-level pop song. It also makes me think about where she has been in the last two years, with Cabello largely out of the pop scene since 2024’s C,XOXO. Time for a comeback, Camila. — M.S.

“Everybody getting’ loose!” Produced by Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, Travis definitely found his pocket on this one. I can see this track growing in popularity over time, and it’s already one of my favorites on the album. You have to crank the volume all the way up for this one. There’s so much electronic-infused chaos packed into the production, making it feel like hip-hop built for the club. It fits flawlessly into the GTA universe. — C.C.

Gunna turned back the clock to the days long before he was running 5Ks and flexed a six-pack as a gym rat. The Atlanta native reunites with frequent collaborator Turbo on the production side for a hard-hitting trap banger that boasts a flow that will sound familiar to early Gunna fans from the days of his Drip or Drown and Drip Season series, when he was still rising through the rap ranks. — M.S.

For all the tenderness with which Kali Uchis and Helado Negro sing to each other, their message couldn’t be more blunt: lárgate (or “f–k off”). The Colombian American singer and Ecuadorian American musician explore the emotional contradictions of a relationship that’s run its course, alternating between wistful reflections and outright dismissal. The sweetness of their vocal interplay almost belies the bitterness of their words. — I.R.

Cardi B will always pop her s—t, and “Don’t Chart” is no different. From the Bronx all the way to Vice City, Cardi is talking her talk! The track marks her second release of 2026, following the arrival of “AH HA” in July. This is Cardi through and through: she’s “still poppin’, still winnin’, [and] you still hatin’.” The bouncy production is packed with flex after flex, touching on confidence, wealth, chart success and designer labels. Thank you, Cardi, for another boastful tongue-in-cheek anthem. — C.C.

“INTERNET $TAR” is a celebration of internet fame, individuality and the freedom to embrace who you are, even when the world doesn’t fully understand or appreciate you. Slayyyter presents herself as influential, memorable and impossible to replicate — which, if you know her, is exactly the point. — C.C.

I imagine Playboi Carti has thousands of songs in a folder on hard drives that he could lend out when needed. Whether it was Carti himself or right-hand producer F1LTHY, they made the right choice going with “Ahh Yea.” For Carti’s standards, “Ahh Yea” leans more into the poppier side of his artistry, and could easily be seen playing on the GTA radio while gamers cruise around Leonida. “Ahh Yea” seems like a holdover from the MUSIC era, and I wish we got more loosies like this from King Vamp. — M.S.

Argentine duo CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso bring their irreverence to the dance floor on “Sexy Magic,” a bouncy, seductive electronic collaboration with British pop artist PinkPantheress, producer Fred again.. and French house veteran Étienne de Crécy. Riding a groovy bassline and shimmering synths, the track pairs Paco’s playful Spanish delivery with PinkPantheress’ breathy English vocals. Psychedelic around the edges and funky at its core, “Sexy Magic” sounds tailor-made for a neon-lit night cruising through Vice City. — I.R.

Travis Scott has been part of the Grand Theft Auto VI rollout every step of the way. Between attending events and making Cactus Jack x GTA merchandise collections, nobody’s been more hyped in hip-hop for the return of the iconic video game series than La Flame.

Scott makes a second appearance on the soundtrack with “Burn This S–t Down,” which sounds as if it has been the most creatively inspired he’s been in the last couple of years. It’s giving me that feeling of a hungry Cactus Jack in the mid-2010s, when he was pushing the boundaries of the genre and making his melodic rage part of hip-hop’s mainstream. That’s a good sign of things to come for La Flame, who should be in album mode for 2027.

“Burn” is a three-part rollercoaster, which he’s experimented with in the past (“SICKO MODE”). Scott plays with melody and then pushes the pace to bar up before turning the title into an eerie chant with an expansive sound that could score a film scene. The final portion will sound familiar to GTA VI gamers, as it was debuted during the explosive final mission of chapter one. — M.S.

New York is in the building! That opening line in the first verse, “You look prettier in person,” hits in this social media era. We all know what it’s like to meet someone in person after finding them online and being happy that they actually look like their pictures — or, in this case, look even better. Boogie, you did your thing with this one, my boy. This is about to go platinum in the crib: “I don’t wanna fight, I wanna dance tonight” — a perfect track for a late-night drive through Vice City.— C.C.

Dua Lipa has proven to be the queen of a soundtrack when she dished out the top 10 Hot 100 bop “Dance the Night” for Barbie in 2023. With an intro that seems to draw from Phil Collins’ “Don’t Lose My Number” and later interpolates KISS’ “I Was Made for Lovin’ You,” the pop star has a penchant for taking songs of yesteryear and making them digestible for today’s audiences. “Go Easy” is no different for the hitmaker, as Dua clears the decks and gears up to launch a new era in the first quarter of ’27. — M.S.

“Flower in a Hurricane” is the preeminent song from GTA VI. In a short time, it’s already essentially become the video game’s theme song, providing the soundtrack to key scenes, clips and compilations going viral on social media. Justice meshes its EDM roots with King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard’s rock while SZA and Kevin Parker join forces to sing about surviving the storm to make it out alive on the other side. It perfectly balances the angst of everything falling apart at any moment on the journey to Vice City glory. — M.S.

“Flower in a Hurricane” is basically Dire Straits’ “Money for Nothing” with special guest Tame Impala. Fully expected to see “Starting from Zero” near the top of the list. Weird ranking…

Alongside its Black Friday Sale, kicking off on Tuesday, Nov. 24, Parke debuts the nostalgic Keepsake Collection, a lineup of previously sold-out archival apparel, plus scrapbook-inspired pieces celebrating 2026 milestones. The best part: The brand-new release is eligible for the 20 percent price drop. #672. Skip the Girl Math: Sitewide Cyber Week Fashion Deals Worth Splurging

Forget tiered discounts and spending minimums. These sitewide Cyber Week fashion deals take the guesswork out of saving.

You're scrolling through social media and your interest is piqued by a Black Friday fashion deal from a brand you normally wouldn't splurge on.

You find the perfect piece and are ready to add it to your cart... only to realize the discount that drew you in doesn't apply to what you want.

It's a shopping scenario that's all too familiar. Between tiered discounts, spending minimums, and category-specific deals, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales often require a fair amount of girl math to figure out...but they shouldn't.

Nobody has time for fine print or mental gymnastics, which is why we compiled the sitewide sales on soft luxury brands that don't require any work:

From Black Friday to Cyber Monday, the seasonal shopping holiday is the ideal time to splurge on pricier brands that are normally out of your budget. Think All Saints, Reformation, Alo, Everlane, Banana Republic, Mejuri, and Larroudé. You can also save at retailers like Nordstrom and Shopbop offering curated selections of splurge-worthy finds.

Because they're all offering sitewide sales, you can confidently shop knowing you're getting a deal, no matter what you add to your cart.

You can shop thousands of fashion deals at Nordstrom, from designer sweaters to rag & bone denim, Burberry bags and Tory Burch shoes, including these dalmatian-print slingbacks for over $100 off.

Everything at Hill House Home is 25% off plus further discounts on select styles. Need an example? Their beloved Nap Dress is 64% off.

Thanks to their sitewide sale, a classic All Saints leather jacket is now within budget. You'll score 30% off (or more) on everything.

Reformation sales are rare, which is why their 25% off everything deal is so enticing. It's a great time to stock up on everything from daily staples to wedding guest dresses.

You can find every soft luxury brand on your wishlist at Shopbop, which is offering 25% off everything with the code HOLIDAY. Veronica Beard to LoveShackFancy, Ganni and Staud.

Now's your chance to score fine jewelry for less at Mejuri. The elevated jewelry brand is offering 30% off everything, including natural and lab grown diamonds, 14k gold, gemstones, and sterling silver.

Everlane is offering an impressive 40% off all their high-quality basics. Shop luxurious fabrics, from merino wool to cashmere.

With 60% off everything, Banana Republic has one of the deepest sitewide discounts we've seen thus far. On select styles, like this timeless wool-blend trench, you can even get an extra 25% off at checkout.

Looking to splurge on a designer bag? Rebecca Minkoff has got you covered with 30% off (almost) everything with the code BFCM30. That includes this structured satchel that you'll reach for daily.

This Black Friday, celebrity-loved athleisure brand Alo is offering you 30% off sitewide, from their coveted sweats to their beloved puffer jackets.

Lululemon's Black Friday sale is live with up to 40% off.

#671. How Amin Joseph Brought “Humanity” to Sonny Liston in ‘The Greatest’

Amazon's Muhammad Ali series rewrites history for one of boxing's biggest heels.

Sonny Liston stood 6’1″ and, in his prime, weighed in at 218 pounds. For Prime Video‘s The Greatest, actor Amin Joseph (Snowfall) added the requisite 23 pounds to his 6’1 (and ½”!) frame to perfectly match that of the former champ.

Joseph proved to be a solid facsimile of Liston in other ways, too. For one, he can really throw hands.

“I grew up fighting,” Joseph told The Hollywood Reporter. “My dad got me into boxing when I was probably around 8 or 9.”

It was probably no coincidence that the formal lessons began shortly after the family moved to Harlem. Related Stories TV Deborah Ann Woll to Reprise 'God of War' Role in Prime Video Series TV Melania Trump Stresses Humanitarian Efforts at Chic Premiere for Two-Episode Series Documentary Follow-Up

Either way, it stuck, and Joseph would box on and off into his college years studying theatre at Howard University. The natural southpaw (not that he told production before landing the role — Liston was a righty) says he had a “knack” for the violent sport, but ultimately was unwilling or unable to “slave [his] mind over” to a coach.

“If he says, ‘Run through a wall.’ If he says, ‘Eat sheetrock’ — you need to slave your mind over to that process,” Joseph said. “[My coach] saw that I already had self-confidence and that I was already shaped as a young man in a certain way, and it was just not worth the investment (for him).”

Boxing is a sport built on length, speed, power, mental fortitude, and in many cases, having an absent (or at least shitty) father. With a present dad at home, Joseph was not looking for what so many younger fighters subconsciously seek. His training had logical limits.

“If [a trainer says], ‘Run at 3 in the morning when it’s raining,’ you don’t need someone going, ‘Well, wait a minute — is that the smartest thing?'” Joseph explained. “You need someone that goes, ‘I’m running.’ Because it could be life or death if you’re in the ring and [a coach] says, ‘I need you to throw this combo.'”

The coach needs the fighter to throw that combo and never question his corner. Joseph, who describes himself as “a thespian through and through,” always saw past the ring.

Liston, for better or worse, was a boxing coach’s dream. Born into a poor sharecropping family, Liston was uneducated and basically tortured by his father. As a young teenager, he ran away from their Arkansas plantation and toward the streets of St. Louis, Missouri. By his early 20s (Liston never really knew his age), Liston was incarcerated.

Not that he minded much: inmates get three meals a day, every single day.

Liston “wanted to be accepted” like “a child” does, Joseph said. So he did as he was told. It was not a lifetime of great advice.

It was in the Missouri State Penitentiary that Liston found boxing. Or really, it was boxing that found Liston. Once more, that would be for better (he’d become World Heavyweight Champion in 1962) and for worse (Liston died under suspicious circumstances in 1970). Throughout his career, Liston was surrounded by unsavory characters.

Before reading Ben Watkins’ scripts, Joseph didn’t know more about Liston than your average… Joseph. He was tangentially aware of the man from the below-pictured infamous KO, which lived on as a mural on the wall of Joseph’s boxing gym (and surely hundreds of others).

Joseph got the education needed from those scripts. He also gained the confidence that he’d have the appropriate screen time to show Liston’s “thought process,” as well as his “humility” and “humbleness.” It is Joseph’s quietest moments in the series that speak the loudest to viewers — not an easy task when playing opposite the loudest and most relentless talker in boxing history.

(Cassius Clay/Muhammad Ali was portrayed with trademark bravado by Jaalen Best. Yes, “Best” was “The Greatest” in what THR TV critic Daniel Fienberg called “a star-making performance.” Fienberg said Joseph “makes Liston into a flawed but tragic figure, ferocious in the ring but eager to find acceptance outside of it,” and calls Liston/Joseph’s talk show-appearance scene “one of the series’ highlights.”)

As heavy as Joseph’s new (pure muscle) weight was, what weighed most on the real Liston was “the shame” of being illiterate throughout adulthood, Joseph said. For Joseph, the greatest selling point of The Greatest is that Watkins doesn’t portray Liston as “a dimwit,” as the media of the time certainly did.

“Literacy isn’t a direct correlation to your intelligence,” Joseph said. “[Liston] is a man that moves in the silence, but when he does talk, it’s so poignant.”

All episodes of The Greatest are currently available on Amazon Prime Video.

#670. TV Ratings: NBA Logs Winning Streak in First Month of the Season

Audiences on national media partners NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are up by 37 percent year to year.

Like a jump shooter who can’t miss, the NBA is on a heater with TV audiences through the first month of its 2026-27 season.

National telecasts of league games on NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are averaging 2.62 million viewers over the season’s first month, based on Nielsen ratings and Adobe Analytics figures for Peacock’s games. That’s a sizable, 37 percent increase over the same time frame last year — the first in the league’s current media rights deal with NBCUniversal, ESPN and Prime Video. Through last week, every national telecast had topped 1 million viewers, the first time that’s happened since 2023. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: CMA Awards Score Seven-Year High TV Streaming Ratings: Rough Week for Original Series, 'From' Remains No. 1 Overall

That’s also the highest mark on record for the first month of an NBA season, excluding lockout-delayed starts in 1999 and 2011 (and with the caveat that changes in Nielsen measurement the past few years have tended to benefit live sports).

NBC’s six national windows lead the way with an average of 4.5 million viewers (including streaming on Peacock), a 27 percent improvement over last season’s first month.. The network’s opening night game between the defending champion New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers (who acquired LeBron James during the offseason) averaged 7.71 million cross-platform viewers.

The first eight games on Prime Video have averaged 2.05 million viewers, and ESPN is at 1.8 million viewers across 13 telecasts. Prime Video has grown by a huge 83 percent year to year, and ESPN’s games are up 13 percent.

Prime Video has the youngest audience of the NBA’s three national media partners (the same is true for Prime relative to other NFL broadcasters); its median viewer age is a little under 46. ESPN and NBC (not including Peacock viewers) have a median age of about 53 for NBA games.

#669. Broadway Box Office: ‘Hamilton’ Rises Back Up to $3M, ‘Here There are Blueberries’ Cracks $1M

'Inter Alia,' starring Rosamund Pike, is also continuing to build momentum.

Hamilton was the top grossing show last week, rising back above $3 million as the industry neared its lucrative holiday week, followed by Other Desert Cities with $2.5 million and the Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell-led Much Ado About Nothing, which still brought in $2 million in a week that included its comped opening night performance.

The Lion King followed with $1.9 million and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child with $1.7 million.

Inter Alia, starring Rosamund Pike, continues to build momentum, bringing in close to $1 million ($993,103) with 100 percent capacity, across its first week of seven performances. The play is set to open Dec. 1.

Here There are Blueberries, a play about museum curators examining previously undiscovered photos from the Holocaust, cracked $1 million for the first time since beginning previews in early November. The show played to close to 100 percent capacity with an average ticket price of $128.

New musical Galileo saw a slight dip in capacity and grosses after lead actor Raúl Esparza missed performances from Nov. 16 through Nov. 18 while recovering from a concussion. The show brought in $699,975 across six performances, and saw capacity fall to 92 percent. The musical is scheduled to open Dec. 6.

Wanted, a new musical which opened Nov. 8, also saw a dip in capacity down to 85 percent, with the show grossing $661,143 across eight performances.

Broadway’s holiday fare has not yet taken off with consumers, with The Blue Man Group playing to 60 percent capacity, illusionist show Now You See Me playing to 77 percent capacity and radio play It’s a Wonderful Life playing to 76 percent.

#668. Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers

Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.

This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.

According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.

Three other men — former head of the Kosovo Intelligence Agency Bashkim Smakaj, former Minister of Justice Hajredin Kuci, and Fadil Fazliu — were also convicted.

Thaci, who was the former political leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the 1998-1999 Kosovo War, is viewed by many in his home country as a hero. His war crimes conviction in September was greeted in Kosovo with anger and dismay.

Thaci has vowed to appeal the war crimes conviction.

His two convictions touch deep sensitivities in Kosovo society. Tuesday's ruling brings renewed attention to the war that ended 27 years ago, the role played by its former leaders, and the continuing debate over justice, individual or collective responsibility for the KLA's war to liberate Kosovo from Serbia, and trust in judicial institutions.

The response from the government of Kosovo was swift.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the government said, "Trust in justice is built not only on the decisions that are made, but also on the manner in which they are reached. Therefore, our commitment to the rule of law and our insistence on the full respect of rights and procedural guarantees are part of the same principled position: Justice must not only be done, but must also be fair, transparent, and credible."

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was established in 2015 by the parliament of Kosovo at the instigation of the European Union and the United States.

The court was created to investigate serious crimes allegedly committed by members of the KLA during and after the Kosovo War.

For security reasons, including concerns about witness intimidation, the court was located in The Hague in the Netherlands.

After Thaci and three others were convicted of war crimes in first instance in September, Kosovo's state authorities established a working group to draft a strategy regarding the appeal proceedings before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The group is chaired by Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca and includes members of Kosovo's parliament.

Prime Minister Albin Kurti has stated that the working group continues to believe that "the first-instance judgment of the Specialist Chambers is unjust, both legally and morally," and that as a result, "the government is working to secure a correction at the appeals level before the Specialist Chambers."

In addition, the parliament of Kosovo is currently considering amendments to the law governing the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The draft law, which is expected to be adopted, envisages narrowing the court's mandate in several areas, including the time period covered by its jurisdiction, limiting the maximum prison sentence to 15 years, allowing sentences to be served in Kosovo, and introducing the possibility of presidential pardons for persons convicted by final court decisions.

How do political analysts and legal experts view the parliament's attempt to amend the law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers before the judicial process involving the four men convicted of war crimes has reached a final verdict?

"From an international perspective, at first glance, this initiative could even be interpreted as an attempt to interfere in the judicial process," said political analyst and university professor Artan Muhaxheri.

"Precisely for this reason, it is essential that Kosovo's political spectrum and its legal experts demonstrate beyond any doubt that this measure does not conflict with Kosovo's international obligations toward the European Union," Muhaxheri told DW, adding that this is the only way to ensure that the desired outcome is achieved and that the initiative does not produce the opposite effect.

"Issues relating to jurisdiction, statutory limits on maximum sentences, and other similar matters must be argued professionally and rigorously, demonstrating that they fully guarantee judicial independence and enjoy solid support within Kosovo's legal system, the same legal system that, first and foremost, established the Specialist Chambers," he said.

Ehat Miftaraj, executive director of the Kosovo Law Institute (IKD), told DW that although the Kosovo Specialist Chambers were established by the Republic of Kosovo itself, "the way the judicial process has unfolded has created the impression that judges, prosecutors and certain international actors have treated not only the accused but also Kosovo itself with distrust, prejudice, and an often condescending approach."

Miftaraj went on to say that reactions and objections in Kosovo to the decisions of the Specialist Chambers are also interpreted and judged in the historical and emotional context of the war and what Kosovo's citizens experienced during and after it.

"In a democratic society, every citizen, including political and institutional representatives, has the right to criticize judicial decisions," he said. "However, there is a fundamental distinction between criticism based on legal arguments and attempts to delegitimize courts or exert influence over judicial proceedings. And here, there is room for criticism of both sides."

#667. Alfonso Ribeiro on the “Wild” Ride of ‘DWTS’ Season 35, Reuniting With Tatyana Ali and Why He Won’t Compete in an All-Winners Season

To commemorate the finale of ‘DWTS,’ Ribeiro chats with THR about the ups-and-downs of season 35, his favorite part about hosting the show and why he can’t predict who will join him in the winners circle on Tuesday night.

Season 35 of Dancing With the Stars marks Alfonso Ribeiro’s fifth season hosting the show, and he has no idea how it will end.

After winning season 19 with Witney Carson, The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air joined the series as a co-host in its 31st season, a year that he believes laid the foundation for the show’s resurgence. “I think we owe a debt of gratitude to Charli D’Amelio doing the show. … Her being literally one of the most popular social media TikTok stars opened the door to an audience that previously didn’t care about this show,” he tells The Hollywood Reporter of what he pinpoints to DWTS’ spike in popularity (and ratings) in recent years. Related Stories TV 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County' Renewed at Hulu TV Lindsay Hubbard Teases 'Summer House' Spinoff 'In the City' Season 2: "Better Than Season One"

The TikTok star certainly brought new eyes to the series, but Ribeiro also refreshed it as host. After one year executing the job alongside Tyra Banks, Julianne Hough stepped in as his co-host, and the duo have remained at the post since. They both bring unique perspectives to DWTS: Ribeiro, as a celebrity who won the series, and Hough, as a former professional dancer and judge.

Ribeiro says there’s so many things that he loves about hosting the show, but one standout is the mentorship he’s able to offer the celebrities. This year, his Fresh Prince sister Tatyana Ali hit the ballroom floor, which he says has been “beautiful for me to experience with her.”

Ali is one of five couples still competing for a chance to win the Len Goodman mirrorball trophy on Tuesday night. Ribeiro admittedly doesn’t know what factors will hold more weight when determining this year’s winner.

“It is quite wild to me because this is a very different season than any other season we’ve ever had,” he says. “So, all of the normal things that we would be able to gauge doesn’t really exist this year.”

One thing Ribeiro hopes is that the portion of the audience spreading hate towards contestants will fade in future seasons. “At the end of the day, this is a dance competition show. This isn’t life or death. No one’s life is changing that greatly from this. It is designed for people to let loose, have some fun and truly enjoy these incredible celebrities,” he adds.

To commemorate the finale of DWTS, Ribeiro chats with THR below about the ups-and-downs of season 35; being in the ballroom and getting the chance to dance with Ali; his opinion on fans who believe celebrities with prior dance experience shouldn’t be cast on the show; and why you won’t ever see him compete on another All-Star (or all-winners) iteration of DWTS.

How does it feel to almost be at the finish line of season 35 of Dancing With the Stars?

This is an incredibly epic season. The numbers, the fans and the interest has been through the roof. We feel really blessed to do something no other show has really ever done in history, which is come back from the brink of extinction to turn around and become the No. 1 show on television. We’ve got a great cast, and they’ve done an incredible job of opening themselves up and allowing America to get to know them. Deena Katz and Conrad Green put a great team together.

The season 35 finale is going to be airing live coast-to-coast for the first time. What do you think that says about the growth and reach of the show that this was so wanted by fans, but also so much so that the affiliates came to an agreement for this to happen?

That’s a major move, right? The only thing on television that does that are sporting events, and the fact that we can move side by side with the NFL and NBA, and people are willing to, on a Tuesday night on the West Coast and Mountain time, come home a little early so that they could watch the show live is quite spectacular when you really think of it. That the affiliates and the network have that much trust in doing this as a finale says that they truly believe that this will work out great for the show and for the sponsors and the companies buying ad time. It says a lot about what they believe in the show.

Do you think that airing the finale live could be a potential test to see how the viewership comes in to see if the show would adapt this live format for a future season?

I can’t really speak on it, obviously, because I don’t know anyone’s thoughts. Anything I say would be conjecture, not anything real. I actually believe that it works the way that it works so far. Of course, we’d love for everyone on the West Coast and everyone in the Mountain time zone to be able to vote for their favorites. I think the interesting way would be to do it on Disney+ and not necessarily on ABC. But the question becomes, does the audience truly support it? And if the audience supports it, then why not, right?

If the numbers end up being as good or better, then of course let’s do it. But there are things that would severely be hampered by that. Technically speaking, ABC News Tonight is the No. 1 broadcast show on Tuesday nights, so you’d be giving up on that for the success of Dancing. The smarter people will make that decision, and we’ll see where that leads us. We’re super excited that we’re getting to experience this particular case. Hopefully all of America and everybody on the West Coast watches it live and we break ratings and voting records.

Tatyana has had such an incredible journey. What has it been like being able to be there and be a part of that journey?

I’ve been trying to get her to do the show for many years, and the timing just wasn’t right. And so happy she did, and really, mostly, so happy for her. It isn’t about me; it’s about her and what she is getting to experience. The little girl I met in 1990, [she’s] all grown up. She’s such a special person. What this show did for me was show America who Alfonso really was, not that character [from Fresh Prince]; same situation for her: getting to experience who Tatyana Ali is and people falling in love with the beautiful human she is.

What was your reaction when she came to you with the idea for you to be a part of her Dedication Night dance in honor of James [Avery]?

It started obviously with the producers asking me the question first. When we finally talked about it, it was already a yes. I expressed my very small concerns of, does that make it look like I’m favoring someone over everyone else, and will that be something that we ultimately have to deal with? And everyone came to the conclusion that that wouldn’t be an issue. The thing that took it over the top for me was that the dedication was to James Avery, and it was bigger than just this show. James Avery played my dad on three different shows, so dedicating it to him felt so right. It was a great opportunity for us to spend extra time together and go through the process of doing a competitive number on the show. I dance all the time on the show, but to be part of a competitive number made it extra special.

You have seen the growth the show has had in the past few years. What do you think it has been about these past two seasons that have really hooked a wider audience and opened the show up to more people?

I actually think it goes back further than the last two seasons. I think we owe a debt of gratitude to Charli D’Amelio for doing the show. Before her season, it was always an older audience. It wasn’t what it is today, and I think that her being literally one of the most popular social media TikTok stars opened the door to an audience that previously didn’t care about this show and always looked at it as, Oh, that’s my grandmother’s show. That’s my parents’ show. It wasn’t their show, and I think Charli D’Amelio made it OK for it to be their show. As the years went along, it just grew and grew, and more people talked about it, and it became this very cool energy that moved through the younger generation. Back in the day, we used to have this term, the “water cooler” TV shows, where people would stand around the water cooler at the office and talk about the show. Well, social media has become the water cooler, and this show has gained on that.

It’s beautiful to watch how the young audience is falling in love with the show. I certainly do hope that the younger audience can be fickle, and know as quickly as they fall in love with something, they fall out of love with it. I’m hoping that they stay in love with it for a while, and recognize that what we’re trying to do is bring love and joy to an audience. I will say that the audience out there that adds a lot of hate, negativity and bullying — I hope that goes away and it becomes more of just love and joy. At the end of the day, this is a dance competition show. This isn’t life or death. No one’s life is changing that greatly from this. It is designed for people to let loose, have some fun and truly enjoy these incredible celebrities.

There has been a lot of chatter and conversation online this season. Has there been one specific conversation online that has specifically stood out to you?

No, I’m not going to say anything specific. What I will say is everyone is entitled to their perspective of what they think the show is, and I would say that for me, it isn’t necessarily a show about people who have no dance experience learning to dance. You do that in Hollywood, it becomes a really short list of people. I look at this show as this is just a bunch of celebrities coming together to learn ballroom dancing. Whether they start with a lot of experience or they start with zero experience, it’s about the journey that they all go on.

What is your favorite part about hosting Dancing With the Stars?

I really do love being almost a mentor to a lot of our celebrities. I go in on Monday and I’m there all day watching every one of the performances and being there as a support system; I’m there for all of it. I’ve been the host of the show, [this year] being my fifth season, and yes, I was a contestant, but I was also a fan from season one on, so I’ve watched almost every person that’s ever done this show in all 35 seasons. That’s really the part that I enjoy: I enjoy being there for them, and it’s a gift that I get to be a part of their journey in some form.

Do you have a favorite number you performed on the show?

My favorite was my Paso Doble to “Turn Down for What.” That was my all-time favorite one. It was a lot of fun to do that. I mean, the music — songs make dances, and you would never think [of doing] a Paso Doble to that song, but yet Witney choreographed a great number having Lindsay [Arnold] on it with us.

Viewers always talk about how they want a potential second all-star season, but something I have always wondered about is an all-winners. If they ever did that and the idea was floated by you, is there any world where you would ever consider doing an all-winners season?

No, and that’s mostly because of the fact that I am the host of the show, and I certainly wouldn’t be giving that job to someone else while I dance again. The answer would be no. You know, we always talk about the all-star season. We always talk about how much fun that would be. The only problem with an all-star season, and especially now, think about how many of our new fans dislike the idea that they have dancers [competing on the show] that are really good dancers. So, you’d literally be making a show that all of those audience members wouldn’t ultimately want to watch. [It’d be] fun for the people doing it, right? But is it fun for that new audience that loves the idea of it being people who couldn’t dance in the beginning?

I think the two fan favorites from this season so far are Connor [Wood] and Tatyana. Tatyana, if she was to win, will be the lowest scoring winner in the history of the show on week one.

That’s this new audience. Tatyana doesn’t make the finale 10 years ago with that audience, because it was never about that. Now you have audience members that really want to see the Guillermos. They want to see the Tatyanas and the Connors and, going back to last season, the Andy Richters. They want to see those people go a long way because, at the end of the day, most of our audience can’t dance, so they’re excited about watching someone who reminds them of themselves achieve something that they would love to do.

I don’t know if I win if I’m on a season now, even though I’m not a trained dancer. Just the idea that I have dance experience, this audience is harder on those people, and I think that’s wrong, personally. That’s my own personal [opinion], not from the show’s perspective. I think it’s wrong because I think if we had 16 people on the show in the beginning who couldn’t dance, I don’t know if that’s an enjoyable show to watch.

I think watching some really great dances, some dances that are mediocre and dances that are not so good, I don’t think that the show would be as successful. I question that audience because I go, man, I think you kind of want your Jenna Dewan’s and your Harry [Shum Jr.]’s and your Charli D’Amelio’s, right? You you want those people on there, and you want to see them continue to get better.

Who do you think will be joining you in the Dancing With the Stars winner’s circle Tuesday night?

Not a clue. I really don’t know. It is quite wild to me because this is a very different season than any other season we’ve ever had. So, all of the normal things that we would be able to gauge doesn’t really exist this year. A lot of people online say that Connor’s getting the most votes, right? OK, but he’s also the lowest-scoring celebrity. So where does that fit? How does that work? How does the scoring system work? All of those questions leave us to, you know, if you were to look at scores through the season so far, Amber [Glenn] and Pasha [Pashkov] and Ezra [Frech] and Daniella [Karagach] are your hands down two of your favorites. Well, we don’t know where they are on the list, so I have no clue. I really don’t. What I will say is, what I’m hoping for is that every one of our celebrities and partners gives the best performances of the season, and then let it fall where it falls.

The season 35 finale of DWTS airs live in every U.S. time zone, with a special three-hour finale on Tuesday at 5 p.m. PT/8 p.m. ET, simulcasting across ABC and Disney+ and streaming the next day on Hulu. Read all of THR‘s DWTS coverage here. This interview was edited and condensed for clarity.

#666. IATSE Reaches Tentative Agreement for Broadway Stagehands

However, the union said its Broadway wardrobe workers are still without a new contract and have voted to authorize a strike.

IATSE Local One, which represents stagehands on Broadway, has reached a tentative agreement with the Broadway League, ahead of the lucrative holiday weeks.

This comes after Local One members had voted to authorize a strike in October, after working on an expired contract since late July. If called, a work stoppage from Local One would have likely put a halt to most Broadway shows. The agreement still needs to be ratified by members of the union, with details of the tentative agreement planned to be available ahead of the union’s December meeting.

However, another local chapter of the union, IATSE Local 764, which represents Broadway dressers and others who work on costumes, still remains without a contract, and voted Sunday to authorize a strike if necessary.

Local 764 members have been bargaining with The Broadway League, a trade association for Broadway producers and general managers, since June. The members’ previous agreement had expired July 26. The League cancelled bargaining sessions scheduled for November 18 and 19, according to IATSE, and Local 764 has been pushing for new dates.

IATSE said the issues still in contention include wages and a gender pay gap that has existed for decades for Broadway wardrobe workers. The field is predominantly female, and has been paid “significantly lower rates than stagehand classifications historically held predominantly by men” according to the union, with Local 764 department heads needing to work 45 percent longer to earn pay comparable to workers in similar department-head roles.

Both Actors’ Equity and the American Federation of Musicians Local 802 also voted to authorize strikes last year, and came very close to doing so, before striking new contracts with the Broadway League.

#665. The brain keeps the score: how trauma leaves molecular scars in cells

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, says Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

The study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” says study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

The study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

The researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’

The amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

The landmark Shenzhou-24 mission is expected to lift off in the next week.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut.

A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week.

The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV).

China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date.

CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time.

Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

One of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions.

China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews.

Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

#663. Netflix Closes $380 Million Acquisition of Radford Studio Center

Netflix is the proud new owner of Radford Studio Center, the 98-year-old soundstage complex that was home to “Gunsmoke,” “The Mary Tyler Moore Show,” and “Seinfeld.”

The streamer is set to close the $380 million acquisition this afternoon, the company said in a statement. The facility last sold to Hackman Capital Partners for $1.85 billion at the peak of the L.A. production market in 2021. The subsequent downturn in production volume and the rise in interest rates forced Hackman to default on its $1.1 billion loan, and ultimately to cede the property to its lender, Goldman Sachs. Related Stories 'NCIS: New York' Sells Across 135 Markets Globally (EXCLUSIVE) Tony Awards Will Remain on CBS Through 2032 Under New Five-Year Deal

Netflix first emerged as a buyer of the 55-acre site in Studio City last spring. Goldman formally took the property back at a foreclosure auction on Tuesday, the final step before the deal with Netflix could close.

The purchase marks a significant investment in Los Angeles for Netflix, which has made similar investments in Albuquerque, N.M., and Fort Monmouth, N.J., in recent years.

“There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California’s film industry,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday. “This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.”

Hackman Capital Partners proposed a $1 billion renovation of the aging Radford lot in 2023. Netflix is expected to continue that ongoing entitlement process with the city as it looks to preserve its development options and its ability to respond to market conditions.

Netflix has its L.A. office headquarters in Hollywood, and has no immediate plans to change that, as several years remain on its office leases. On top of the $380 million purchase price, Netflix also paid a 5.5% transfer tax due to the city’s Measure ULA.

Filming will proceed as usual on the lot. Cinelease will serve as the production equipment provider.

#662. Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock

Deep beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists have uncovered a surprising world of tiny animals living inside metal-rich rocks that take millions of years to form. These rocks, known as polymetallic nodules, contain miniature cracks and cavities that provide shelter for creatures smaller than a millimeter.

Although they may look like ordinary stones, these nodules offer something unusual in the deep ocean. They create hard surfaces in an environment dominated by soft mud, while their internal spaces provide additional habitats for marine life.

Polymetallic nodules are dark, roughly fist-sized formations made largely of iron and manganese oxides. They grow at an extraordinarily slow pace, often adding only a few millimeters over a million years. Found at ocean depths ranging from 4,000 to 6,000 meters, they can remain on the seafloor for millions of years.

Researchers set out to investigate the tiny organisms living within these ancient formations and determine how important the nodules are to deep-sea biodiversity.

Dr. Tanja Stratmann, a deep-sea ecologist and one of the study's three lead authors, explains: "In our study we show that the sizes of cracks inside the nodules are large enough to provide home to animals that are smaller than a millimeter in size."

Hundreds of Tiny Animals Found Inside a Single Rock

To explore these hidden habitats, the research team collected nodules from the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, a vast region of the central Pacific Ocean. They used specialized sampling equipment, including box corers that collect sections of the seafloor and remotely operated diving robots capable of working at extreme depths.

Back in the laboratory, the researchers carefully opened the nodules and extracted the tiny animals concealed within their cracks and crevices.

The results revealed an unexpectedly rich community of marine life. Across 244 nodules, the team identified 4,139 individual animals. Each nodule contained an average of 17 animals, but one particularly crowded specimen sheltered an astonishing 245 individuals.

The discovery shows that these rocks are more than simple surfaces where marine organisms can attach themselves. Their intricate internal structures create three-dimensional living spaces, allowing animals to inhabit protected areas within the nodules themselves.

Dr. Coral Diaz-Recio Lorenzo explains: "The crevices in the polymetallic nodules function as small shelters and provide home to animals that we do not encounter in the soft sediment of the seafloor."

Hidden Ecosystems Unlike Those on the Surrounding Seafloor

Although the nodules contained fewer animals than the surrounding muddy sediment, their contribution to deep-sea life was still substantial.

For roundworms (nematodes), the number living inside the nodules amounted to approximately 10% of the number found in the surrounding sediment. For tiny crustaceans (copepods), the figure was about 25%.

However, the most important finding was not simply how many animals the researchers discovered. It was how different the communities inside the rocks were from those living in the nearby mud.

Genetic analyses revealed that the animals inhabiting the nodules formed distinctive communities. Remarkably, these communities remained highly similar across locations separated by large distances (up to 1,000 km), even though they differed significantly from the organisms found in the surrounding seafloor sediment.

This suggests that polymetallic nodules support specialized habitats that are not easily replaced by other parts of the deep ocean. Their cracks and cavities offer living conditions that certain organisms appear to depend on.

Deep-Sea Mining Could Destroy These Ancient Habitats

The findings raise serious concerns about the potential environmental consequences of deep-sea mining.

Polymetallic nodules contain economically valuable metals, including nickel, cobalt, and copper. These resources have attracted interest in industrial mining operations that would collect the nodules directly from the ocean floor.

However, removing the rocks would also eliminate the miniature habitats they contain, along with the animals living inside them.

One example is Thurammina sp. 1, a single-celled organism found particularly frequently within the nodules. This species appears especially well adapted to the sheltered spaces inside the rocks, making it an example of the specialized life that could be threatened by their removal.

The problem is that these habitats cannot quickly recover. Because polymetallic nodules require millions of years to develop, new ones would not form within a human lifetime. Mining could therefore eliminate ecosystems that would take geological timescales to replace.

Prof. Sabine Gollner warns: "Our findings point out that commercial mining may result in an irreversible loss of undescribed and unique biodiversity associated to nodules. This needs to be considered in environmental management of deep-sea mining."

Scientists Race to Understand What Could Be Lost

The discovery highlights an often overlooked aspect of ocean conservation. Protecting deep-sea ecosystems requires more than safeguarding large, visible animals. It also means considering the microscopic and nearly microscopic organisms that inhabit specialized environments hidden within the seafloor.

An important question remains unanswered: If deep-sea mining destroys these nodule communities, could some species disappear entirely?

Researchers still need to determine whether organisms that depend on the nodules also inhabit other parts of the ocean. If certain species are restricted to these habitats, removing the nodules could potentially contribute to their global extinction.

Understanding where these animals live and how widely they are distributed will be essential for identifying areas that need protection and evaluating the potential ecological damage caused by deep-sea mining.

To investigate further, Dr. Tanja Stratmann is currently participating in an international research expedition to the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, where scientists are continuing to study the ecosystems associated with polymetallic nodules.

This expedition and other follow-up investigations are independently funded through the JPIOcean projects MiningImpact 2 and 3.

The findings reveal that even a single rock on the deep ocean floor can support a surprisingly complex community of life. As interest in harvesting the ocean's mineral resources grows, scientists are working to understand these hidden ecosystems before habitats that took millions of years to form are permanently lost.

Materials provided by MARUM - Center for Marine Environmental Sciences, University of Bremen. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

JAXA has abandoned its plan to rendezvous with the asteroid 1998 KY26, switching to a high-speed flyby of 2015 BM510.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters.

The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu. Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune.

But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan.

But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. The spacecraft was scheduled to rendezvous with, and attempt to land on, the tiny, 36-foot-wide (11 meters) near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, but trouble with the aging spacecraft's engines has forced a change of plan.

The spacecraft will instead target 2015 BM510, another tiny asteroid. And there will be no landing: Hayabusa2 is scheduled to make a high-speed flyby of the near-Earth object in April 2028.

The decision was announced at a Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) press conference on Tuesday (Nov. 17), a day after a Cabinet Office space policy subcommittee meeting. The final functioning thruster out of Hayabusa2's four ion engines suffered a malfunction in mid-August, according to JAXA officials, while a sensor detected unexpected erosion of the spacecraft's surface during its long voyage in space.

"The deterioration of the onboard equipment ... is becoming increasingly evident," Japan Times quoted Yuya Mimasu, team leader of the extended mission, as saying.

Despite losing the opportunity to land on KY26, the Hayabusa2 mission has been a huge success for JAXA, and the new direction promises its own intrigues. Asteroid 2015 BM510 has already attracted interest; it's the primary target of a proposal for the European Space Agency's mini-Fast mission series. Scientists describe the body as a D-type asteroid, meaning it's thought to be organic-rich and comet-like, and may have originated in the outer solar system.

Around the same time as Hayabusa2 conducts its high-speed flyby in April 2028, JAXA is also scheduled to launch its next asteroid mission, Destiny+. Launching along with ESA's Ramses mission to study Apophis, Destiny+ will first make a flyby of the infamous asteroid ahead of its very close approach to Earth in 2029 before heading to asteroid 3200 Phaethon, the parent body of the Geminid meteor shower.
